info.title: Dezfil API
info.description: Upload files, query them with SQL, compose styled map layers, and publish read-only shareable views. Every capability the UI offers is one of these documented calls; the whole journey can be driven headlessly. Protected operations require a current cookie session or account bearer token. Every map, dataset, workflow, connection and project has one owner and is private to its owner unless a project shares it: a project's owner gives people the viewer or editor role, and they reach the project and everything filed in it, whoever owns it. A viewer reads; an editor also changes the content of its maps and workflows and runs its workflows; deletion, publication, sharing and transfer stay the owner's, and datasets change only by their owner. Connections are never shared, and standalone jobs, renders and downloads stay with the account that started them. Administrators have no additional content access. Dataset and connection names are owner-local: in SQL another person's reachable dataset is <sql name>.<dataset>, and a map's or workflow's SQL reads in its SQL home. Unreached and missing resources share the same refusal. Instance catalogues and saved palettes remain shared. User SQL reads named datasets only; direct or indirect file reads and path discovery are refused. Cookie mutations require the same trusted Origin. Identity-bearing responses, including authentication refusals, are private, no-store. Only entry, readiness and the token-scoped read-only published projection permit anonymous access. Maps and workflows have one durable editRevision, paired with state on document, child and list reads. Covered writes require X-Edit-Revision (MCP expected_revision); order writes and chain the accepted JSON result. Missing or malformed revisions return 400 invalid_request. Stale revisions return 409 stale_revision: This item has changed. Reload it before trying again. Refusal changes nothing. Reload explicitly and compose a new edit, never replay an old payload under a fresh token. This breaks unversioned writers and clients expecting bodyless covered successes. Whole-document deletion has no surviving revision. Viewport-only saves, picture refresh and run cancellation keep their documented exceptions. Attribution names the last accepted actor, not the owner; legacy authors can be unknown. Shared map undo retains original authors. Run starts use the plan revision; admitted runs track executable definitions, preserving concurrent layout and lifecycle changes. Unsupported methods on documented paths return 405 method_not_allowed with an exact Allow header after authentication. HEAD is bodyless and OPTIONS reports Allow.

tags.name: Layers
tags.description: A layer is SQL + name + style.

tags.name: Sketches
tags.description: Drawing as data: a draw session becomes one ordinary GeoParquet dataset plus one layer on its map. Features carry a stable id and drawn kind; the owning-layer cascade deletes layer and dataset together and is deliberately not undoable.

tags.name: Operations
tags.description: Spatial and data operations. Each produces a durable dataset with recorded provenance; the catalog describes the verbs this instance offers.

tags.name: Recipes
tags.description: A recipe is a named, ordered list of steps whose dependencies point only backwards. It records what each step was made from, so when the data underneath changes the answer to 'what is now out of date' is a fact rather than a guess. Recipes are workspace objects like datasets — not owned by a map.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: An optional named set over maps, workflows and datasets. A map or workflow is in at most one project; a dataset can be in several. Project workflows are workflow-origin recipes; builder-origin recipes cannot be project members. A project is also the one boundary of sharing: its owner gives people the viewer or editor role, and they reach everything filed in it, whoever owns it. Filing never changes who owns a resource or what a plain table name means in a map's or workflow's SQL. Deleting one dissolves the set, ends every person's reach through it and deletes nothing.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Finished maps and workflow examples with their data, shipped in the image or listed by the template catalogue, for every signed-in account. A template belongs to no one and is listed among no one's maps, workflows or datasets.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Drive Dezfil from AI agents: the documented API surface, served as MCP tools, plus the in-product assistant.

get.description: The instance name, sign-in message, lost-password contact, landing page, the shortest password a password chosen on these screens needs, and setup availability. The landing page value does not change navigation. Before setup, the legacy display name may prefill Name. Never returns a signed-in person's identity or account preferences. Private, no-store.

post.description: At most 65,536 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `request_body_too_large` before JSON parsing. Cookie mutations and entry submissions require an Origin matching the trusted request origin. Explicit bearer authentication does not use cookies. Responses are private, no-store. Atomically creates the sole initial admin, adopts legacy preferences and establishes a cookie session. Once any account exists, setup_complete refuses further creation. Password derivations share two active slots and at most eight waiters: six ordinary and two reserved protected, each waiting at most five seconds. FIFO within each class; validated links and signed-in current-password work are protected, including the second password-change derivation. Protected work takes the next free slot but at most one active slot, even with ordinary slots idle. Ordinary work may use both; running work is never pre-empted. A fourth simultaneous protected caller is refused at once and may retry immediately without a login lockout; the busy response advises a one-second retry. Known and unknown sign-ins are ordinary. Overflow or deadline answers authentication_busy. Cancellation removes waiters; native work owns its slot until it settles. Recovery issuance derives nothing.

patch.description: At most 65,536 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `request_body_too_large` before JSON parsing.  Password derivations share two active slots and at most eight waiters: six ordinary and two reserved protected, each waiting at most five seconds. FIFO within each class; validated links and signed-in current-password work are protected, including the second password-change derivation. Recovery issuance derives nothing.Cookie or bearer authentication is required. Cookie mutations require the same trusted Origin. Responses, including refusals, are private, no-store. Changes only your own name or email. An email change requires currentPassword and replaces the sign-in email. Duplicate emails return email_taken, regardless of case or surrounding whitespace. Missing or incorrect current passwords return current_password_required. Current-password checks on password and email changes share one allowance per account, apart from sign-in accounting: the Failed sign-ins per account count (security.failedPerAccount, five by default) within a fixed fifteen minutes. Missing or incorrect current passwords count; busy refusals, failing password work and a caller who leaves before the check starts do not; a caller who leaves after it starts keeps that place taken until the window ends. Concurrent checks never exceed what is left. Past the count, checks return rate_limited with Retry-After, retryAfter seconds and retryAt (ISO timestamp) before any password work. A correct current password clears this count and leaves sign-in's untouched; a sign-in clears only its own. The complete patch is validated before any write; account identity, role and status cannot be submitted.

Returns only the account identity already visible in Users, totals per owned kind and distinct other active people whose present reach shrinks. Never returns private names, project references, rosters or content. The opaque confirmation is bound to the target, requesting admin, eligibility generation, inventory identities, publication links, grants and filings. Same-count swaps, publication changes and a reactivate/deactivate cycle invalidate it; unrelated surviving-document edits do not. A pending deletion returns its identifier and unfinished state instead. Self and active-target refusals are identical to deletion. This read erases nothing.

post.description: Requires a current admin account through a cookie session or bearer token. Cookie mutations require the same trusted Origin. Responses, including refusals, are private, no-store. Deletion is permanent erasure of the account and everything it owns, wherever filed; shared reach and published links end. Owned projects dissolve and surviving members' work becomes unfiled. No handover occurs. Deactivation keeps shared reads, copies, runs and links. Except for never-redeemed invitations, deletion purges all geocode, isochrone and Overpass answer caches; later requests contact providers again. The identifying SQL name stays reserved forever for an ever-active account; completion frees its email. Others' derived datasets and stored SQL, lineage and run text remain theirs and can retain names or personal text. Issued private copies keep their shipped lifetime; completion waits for prepared files to settle or expire and cleanup to finish. Recorded input evidence identifies affected foreign card images, tiles, renders and prepared files; existing unattributed card images owned by others remain. Deleting a workflow removes its run records while its output datasets remain. Host snapshots, backups, logs, providers, browser-local SQL/conversations, exports, downloaded files and databases written through connections are outside erasure; restoring a backup can revive data and credentials. This is neither disk-remanence erasure nor anonymization. Pending or needs-retry is unfinished, never completed success: use status or Finish deleting with the same identifier; the account and its work stay inaccessible. Finishing rewrites the whole metadata store and pauses every response. An outside database reader or insufficient free working space on the data volume or SQLite temporary filesystem can prevent compaction; release the reader or restore space, then Finish deleting safely with the same identifier. Resumes the accepted deletion, including after restart, without changing its identifier or repeating completed dissolution. Concurrent requests join the same work. An unreadable record returns 409 deletion_unreadable without changing any files. Completed identifiers return 404 not_found.

x-confirmation.consequence: This permanently erases the account and everything it owns. Other people lose shared access and published links stop working. This cannot be undone.

get.description: Requires a current admin account through a cookie session or bearer token, rechecked on every call. Responses, including refusals, are private, no-store. Returns every instance and platform definition with its effective value, source, stored value (including a shadowed value), lock and invalid-override state. A non-empty environment variable locks the setting even when invalid; invalid numeric overrides use the default without returning the override text. Empty numeric overrides are absent; a set empty assistant model list retains its default model alone. Environment changes require a restart. Provider keys report set or not set; the encryption key reports environment, data-directory or not-yet-present. Address value and defaultValue expose scheme and host only, never user information, paths, queries or fragments; malformed addresses report set and unreadable. A service address or the satellite tile template an admin stored reads as set with its scheme and host, or as set and unreadable once the instance's encryption key no longer opens it; its storedValue is always null. The satellite tile template in effect, stored or set by DEZFIL_SATELLITE_URL, also reads with userInformation true while it carries a user name or password, which is never given: the imagery is not drawn from such an address. The satellite credit an admin stored reads as stored while DEZFIL_SATELLITE_ATTRIBUTION is unset, and as the variable's, with the stored credit as storedValue, while it is set. The template catalogue's address (templatesCatalogueUrl) reads as a service address does; while DEZFIL_TEMPLATES_CATALOGUE names a folder on this server instead of an http or https address, it reads as set with folder true, and the folder's path is never given. Trusted engine memory (trustedMemoryMb) defaults to 3072 MB and Bytes drawn per layer (renderCapBytes) to 134217728 bytes; both are deployment-controlled and reject writes. Data processing time limit (dataProcessingTimeoutS) defaults to 3600 seconds, accepts stored whole seconds from 60 to 21600, and resets with null. Trusted imports, refreshes, geometry and sketch changes, template installation and export conversion use the Data processing time limit. Trusted work shares the configured memory budget and a dedicated scratch allowance of four times that value; restart clears abandoned spill. Exhaustion answers engine_memory_exceeded, naming memory or scratch and DEZFIL_TRUSTED_MEMORY_MB. Upload reception and processing each use the value admitted when reception begins, with separate deadlines. Layer renders and dataset map features count their complete inline answer against Bytes drawn per layer as it is built; above it a layer takes its tile road or answers the errored layer render_bytes_exceeded, and dataset map features answer ok:false with a reason. Slider, Overture and OpenStreetMap previews and the sketch features read count theirs too and answer 422 render_bytes_exceeded above it. The built-in documentedDefault stays as documented, including any path. Contextual defaults carry a rule when there is no single address or value. The read generates no key, writes no configuration file, contacts no service and initializes no engine. Capacities report admitted geocode rows and travel-time origins per run, without promising a configured provider. Also returns the fixed maximum image dimension, package version, stable process start time and warnings when the effective query timeout is at or above the run timeout. Services report each provider cache (geocode, isochrone, overpass) with the bytes its answers take, how many it holds and its budget in MB, and the Overture release list this process keeps: how many releases, the newest and when it was listed, or not listed yet. Parts report each part of this server, starting nothing and running no program: the query engine's library version, whether the engine has started and the extensions it loaded; whether the tile builder and the image renderer's browser are executable files where their settings point, by a file check, the tile builder's version once this server has run it, and Images at once; the metadata database's file name. basemapStyles is the basemap library, oldest first, hidden styles included: each style's id, name, address, credit, whether it is offered and when it was added.

patch.description: At most 65,536 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `request_body_too_large` before JSON parsing. Requires a current admin through cookie or bearer authentication, rechecked inside the write transaction on every call. Cookie mutations require the same trusted Origin; an admin bearer token calls directly with no additional scope or approval step. Responses, including refusals, are private, no-store. Submit only editable keys; omitted keys stay unchanged and null clears a stored value. The complete body is validated against the committed configuration under one write lock. A refusal or failed commit changes nothing. Non-editable keys answer 400 invalid_request as read-only regardless of their environment. A non-empty environment variable locks an editable setting, including invalid overrides and null writes. A locked editable key answers 409 setting_locked, taking precedence over 400 invalid_request for unknown, non-editable, wrong-kind, non-whole, out-of-range, over-length or invalid-choice entries, a site list entry that is not http or https with a host and an optional port, a resulting queryTimeoutS at or above operationTimeoutS, a resulting security.failedPerAddress below security.failedPerAccount, and a resulting publishing.embedding of listed with no publishing.embedSites. Messages identify all failing known keys and their reasons, unknown keys by their entry position and a refused site by its position, without echoing arbitrary input. The sign-in counts, and embedding with its sites, are checked when a body changes either side. An existing environment timeout mismatch is reported in warnings and blocks no unrelated change. Concurrent different-key edits both land; the last accepted value wins on one key. There is no stale-write rejection or Undo. Stored changes apply live to new work; admitted work keeps its budget. Lowered concurrency cancels nothing, increased concurrency wakes waiters after commit, and lowered queue limits keep accepted waiters. Public limits apply against the existing window count. Environment changes need a restart. Returns the same configuration as the read, with the same secret and address disclosure rules. No secret is accepted. The four service addresses (geocoderUrl, isochroneUrl, overpassUrl, s3Endpoint), the satellite imagery's tile template (satelliteUrl) and the template catalogue's address (templatesCatalogueUrl) are write-only: each is stored encrypted and read back as its scheme and host alone; a refusal names the key and never repeats the address. The catalogue's address is http or https here: a folder on the server is named by DEZFIL_TEMPLATES_CATALOGUE alone. The template must also hold {z}, {x} and {y}, a refusal naming the ones missing, and carry no user name or password, refused before any lookup with a sentence saying the imagery is not drawn from such an address and the key belongs in the path or the query. Before the write, an address is also refused (400 invalid_request, with the egress policy's own sentence) when that policy would refuse a request to it now, a template with each placeholder filled with a digit: a literal in loopback, private, carrier-grade, link-local or metadata, unique-local, unspecified, multicast or reserved space, mapped and NAT64 forms included, or a name all of whose addresses resolve there, unless DEZFIL_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST names it. A name that does not resolve at save is kept; every request to the address is checked again. The embedded assistant asks for confirmation before calling on pages admitting writes; SQL and workflow assistants refuse this update. MCP advertises that policy and adds no confirmation step.

x-confirmation.consequence: These settings apply to the whole instance. Limits affect new work; admitted work keeps its budget. There is no Undo.

post.description: Requires a current admin through cookie or bearer authentication, rechecked on every call. Cookie requests require the same trusted Origin; an admin bearer token calls directly. Responses, including refusals, are private, no-store. Sends the service one fixed request at its address in effect, never one given here: geocode (the address finder) one search for a fixed place, isochrone (travel time) one area on foot round a fixed point for the shortest band, overpass (OpenStreetMap) the smallest Overpass query, overture a listing of the releases, s3 one request to the S3 address's root without credentials, satellite one fixed low-zoom tile (zoom 3, x 4, y 2) at the imagery's tile template within 10 seconds, passing when the answer is an image (a template carrying a user name or password is refused, with the sentence a save refuses it with, and nothing is sent), templates the template catalogue's index, read as a refresh reads it within the link import's time bound (DEZFIL_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_S), or from the folder DEZFIL_TEMPLATES_CATALOGUE names, passing with how many templates it lists, an index this server would refuse being unexpected_answer. It goes the way the service's own requests go: through the egress check, redirects included, and after the gap between requests for the address finder and travel time. It reaches outside this server and stores nothing: no setting changes and no cache is read or written, except that the Overture Test keeps the release list it finds, as Check now does. A second Test of a service while one runs gets the same answer from the same request. A stored address the instance's key no longer opens is refused with service_address_unreadable, as the service refuses it. Walks the data folder and answers, for each kind of file, the bytes its files take and how many there are: tables (dataset files the metadata registers), tile_archives (archives with a tile record and what they were built from), service_caches (the three caches' answers), thumbnails (map card images), profile_pictures (each person's current picture), templates (downloaded templates, and the copies of an installed template's data the query engine reads), metadata_database (the database and its journal files), leftover_files (what the next restart's sweeps would remove: upload, download and tile scratch, staged project exports with their ownership records, table files no dataset or installed template uses, archives no layer uses, unfinished thumbnail writes, pictures that are no one's current picture; it includes work in progress) and other (the rest, such as the key file and the server's records); with every kind together and the free and total space on the folder's volume. Each file counts once, however many names it has. It takes names and sizes, which files the metadata references and which the installed templates' records name, opening no other file and following no link, and answers no name, owner, account, map, dataset, path or file name. One walk runs at a time: a read during a walk gets that walk's answer, and a read within 30 seconds of it gets the same answer, unless a service cache was cleared since the walk began: a Clear ends a walk under way at once, the reads already joined to it getting what it had counted, and a read after the Clear never gets a walk begun before it but joins one fresh walk. A copied dataset's source reads `template`, with the template's id and version in its sourceParams, and it is never refreshed. The map's card images are the template's pictures, saved after the copy with evidence naming the copied datasets; when they cannot be saved the copy stands and its card shows the placeholder until the map's first capture. A second copy makes a second project of the same name with its datasets suffixed, the first unchanged; copies made at once each land whole under distinct names. Refused, coded, with nothing created: 404 template_not_listed for a version neither installed nor listed; 409 template_not_installed; 409 templates_catalogue_off for a version not installed while an admin has turned the catalogue off; 400 service_address_unreadable for a saved address the instance's key no longer opens; 422 template_reference_unbound for a layer naming a dataset the copy does not make, or a step reading one; 422 template_record_mismatch and the template reader's other codes for an installed version that changed on disk; 400 invalid_request for a body that is not an optional name and version; 413 request_body_too_large. Answers the project with its members.

get.description: A dataset is reached by its owner and by the owner and people of every project it is filed in. Lists, schema discovery and counts cover exactly the reached datasets and name each one's owner and the name the caller would type for it: the plain name for the caller's own, <sql name>.<name> for another owner's. Another owner's dataset is shown without connection facts and without links to what the caller cannot reach: a PostGIS snapshot shows its origin kind, with neither its connection nor its remote schema and table. A bare dataset name in a path or parameter is the caller's own dataset. On dataset reads, features, downloads and operation parameters, another owner's dataset the caller reaches is addressed by its qualified name, and in a /api/tables path also by its identifier; changing one by any address answers forbidden. Datasets change, refresh and go only by their owner; administrators reach nothing more. Upload and sketch suffixes ignore other accounts' names. Unreached and missing datasets, maps and project references return not_found before source or artifact access; a refused change leaves resources unchanged. Refresh and geometry changes preserve the dataset's identity and owner and recheck account activity at commit. For file uploads and URL imports only. Malformed/unknown fields and incompatible types answer 400 invalid_request; missing columns answer 400 column_unavailable. Unusable choices answer 422 geometry_choice_invalid with issues. Post-commit cleanup failure does not reverse success. A saved manual geometry choice on a URL import replays against fresh source columns before automatic conversion, survives restart, and commits with the artifact and geometryRecord. Clear removes the override: the next refresh resumes automatic recognition, records its fresh result and resets geometry mode to unmodified. get.description: Readiness reports whether socket provenance is installed, the data directory is usable, and, once a query has started the query engine that runs SQL, whether that engine can serve. post.description: Created resources belong to the authenticated account. Submitted owner identities cannot assign or transfer ownership. A dataset is reached by its owner and by the owner and people of every project it is filed in. Lists, schema discovery and counts cover exactly the reached datasets and name each one's owner and the name the caller would type for it: the plain name for the caller's own, <sql name>.<name> for another owner's. Another owner's dataset is shown without connection facts and without links to what the caller cannot reach: a PostGIS snapshot shows its origin kind, with neither its connection nor its remote schema and table. A bare dataset name in a path or parameter is the caller's own dataset. On dataset reads, features, downloads and operation parameters, another owner's dataset the caller reaches is addressed by its qualified name, and in a /api/tables path also by its identifier; changing one by any address answers forbidden. Datasets change, refresh and go only by their owner; administrators reach nothing more. Upload and sketch suffixes ignore other accounts' names. Unreached and missing datasets, maps and project references return not_found before source or artifact access; a refused change leaves resources unchanged. Refresh and geometry changes preserve the dataset's identity and owner and recheck account activity at commit. multipart/form-data with exactly one file part, named `file` — a request with several file parts, or a file under another field name, is refused without importing anything. To upload a batch, repeat the request once per file. Accepts GeoParquet, GeoJSON, CSV, Shapefile (as .zip), GeoPackage, and KML/KMZ. A container holding several spatial layers creates one table per layer; the answer enumerates them. Reception and processing each get the Data processing time limit captured when receiving begins, with separate deadlines. Changing the setting during receipt changes neither budget. No body byte for 60 seconds, including before the first byte, answers 408 upload_stalled. Reception or processing expiry answers 408 data_processing_timeout, naming the work and admitted limit. The first refusal is delivered without waiting for another byte or draining the body; the refused connection closes within five seconds. Incomplete reception cancels on departure and removes its partial file. Complete uploads continue processing after departure. CSV geometry recognition uses names first, in order: a text column named wkt/geometry/geom is parsed as WKT; lon/lat, lng/lat, long/lat, or longitude/latitude pairs become point geometry when each member is numeric or contains no non-blank values; when a member qualifies only by being blank, a numeric prefixed pair takes precedence. Empty and quoted-empty fields are blank; whitespace-only text is not. A row missing either member has null geometry. A prefixed pair (origin_lon/origin_lat, pickup_longitude/…) becomes the point when it is the origin pair or the only one. Safe prefixed x/y retains that name priority; bare x/y and easting/northing are weak candidates. Unsafe names yield to the next eligible name, then to content. A named WKT column with sampled non-null values but none readable stays weak with an unreadable reason and retains its source text; a strong content reading of that same column may apply instead. Content recognition samples the first 1,000 reader rows, excluding NULLs from each format's denominator. WKT/EWKT, GeoJSON geometry objects (not Features or FeatureCollections), WKB hex including EWKB SRIDs, and validated H3 cells are supported. An H3 cell becomes its boundary polygon; unavailable validation yields only an unvalidated weak hint. A content column is strong only when every sampled non-null value reads in that format, with at least one readable value. When some but not all read, it is weak with its sampled count. Strong ties use source column order. Content numeric pairs are always weak; unnamed pairs need at least 50% of complete sampled rows in a possible degree orientation, and ambiguous axes remain marked. The chosen mapping is checked over the entire input for finite longitude/x in [-180,180] and latitude/y in [-90,90], including every geometry vertex and values after the sample. A consistent declared CRS is reprojected to WGS84 under the file-ingest contract; conflicting declarations and untransformable SRIDs stay weak with reasons. Unknown declarations never become a WGS84 assumption. Undeclared degree-compatible WKT/WKB and eligible named pairs assume WGS84; GeoJSON and H3 are inherently WGS84 and declarations are not assumptions. Selected unreadable non-null values keep their rows with NULL geometry and a full-input unreadable count; missing inputs do not increment that count. Content roads retain source columns and add a distinct geometry column; named WKT keeps its replacement behavior. The geometryCandidates evidence retains alternatives, source identities, sample observations, axis roles, CRS and reasons. The geometryRecord identifies the applied choice, source CRS stance and full unreadable count, persisted for table inspection. Legacy records remain absent. Without an eligible mapping the CSV lands as a plain table with all source rows and columns and no CRS assumption. Local and URL CSV imports share these rules; refresh replaces automatic evidence with its artifact atomically, and failure keeps both old versions. A CSV whose detected column names betray a broken read: a name containing a comma (the header was never split), or most names numeric or blank (the first data row was taken as the header) imports with `headerSuspect: true`. The warning is advisory: it refuses nothing and changes nothing about recognition. MCP accepts at most 16,777,216 bytes for the entire JSON envelope, including base64. The raw file must be below 12 MiB, reduced by envelope and metadata overhead and by the configured upload cap. For canonical base64, subtract the serialized empty-content envelope bytes from 16,777,216, round down to whole groups of four, and allow three file bytes per group.

post.description: At most 16,777,216 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `request_body_too_large` before JSON parsing. Created resources belong to the authenticated account. Submitted owner identities cannot assign or transfer ownership. A dataset is reached by its owner and by the owner and people of every project it is filed in. Lists, schema discovery and counts cover exactly the reached datasets and name each one's owner and the name the caller would type for it: the plain name for the caller's own, <sql name>.<name> for another owner's. Another owner's dataset is shown without connection facts and without links to what the caller cannot reach: a PostGIS snapshot shows its origin kind, with neither its connection nor its remote schema and table. A bare dataset name in a path or parameter is the caller's own dataset. On dataset reads, features, downloads and operation parameters, another owner's dataset the caller reaches is addressed by its qualified name, and in a /api/tables path also by its identifier; changing one by any address answers forbidden. Datasets change, refresh and go only by their owner; administrators reach nothing more. Upload and sketch suffixes ignore other accounts' names. Unreached and missing datasets, maps and project references return not_found before source or artifact access; a refused change leaves resources unchanged. Refresh and geometry changes preserve the dataset's identity and owner and recheck account activity at commit. Queries the configured Overpass endpoint and lands the result as GeoParquet tables split by geometry class (stem_points / stem_lines / stem_polygons, non-empty classes only) — one import group with one stored query, refreshed together. Provide selectors (tag filters like ["amenity=restaurant"]) with a bbox, or a raw OverpassQL query (the escape hatch; overpass-turbo's {{bbox}} is honoured). Either way the server applies its safety envelope (output format, timeout, size). Tags land as one JSON column plus promoted plain columns for name and the queried keys. Identical queries within the cache window do not re-hit the endpoint.

ql.description: Raw OverpassQL (alternative to selectors); the safety envelope replaces any declared settings.

ring.description: Drawn polygon [[lng, lat], …] (≤ 500 points) — alternative to bbox; becomes an Overpass poly filter.

geometry.description: A GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon (≤ 20,000 vertices) as the area — e.g. a feature from an existing table. Each part becomes an Overpass poly filter; holes apply in the post-fetch within filter. Takes precedence over ring/bbox.

semantics.description: within keeps only features entirely inside the drawn shape (enforced server-side after geometry assembly — Overpass itself returns intersections); the default is intersect.

projectId.description: The project every created table joins; omitted or null, unfiled. An unknown project refuses before the source is contacted. It must be a project the caller owns or edits, whose owner is active: one the caller only views refuses with forbidden, and one they cannot reach refuses as an unknown one.

201.description: Created tables, one per non-empty geometry class.

Hidden or missing connection references return not_found before reading credentials, contacting the source or changing stored health. The caller cannot supply credentials, source SQL, or a row limit. Caller departure prevents later stages of this preview and discards late results (empty HTTP 499). Every source connection opened by the preview attachment has a 30-second per-statement ceiling; timeout answers HTTP 408 query_timeout. A departed caller's blocked source statement runs to that ceiling: the interrupt is observed between scan chunks and cannot reach a scan blocked in a libpq read. The aborted case's 35-second bound on responsive source and transport is met by the ceiling and is not evidence of interrupt propagation. The preview records nothing about the connection: neither its success nor any failure, cancellation or timeout changes the stored health, which answers for the last connection test, import or refresh. Connection tests, catalogue reads, imports and refreshes keep their existing limits.

post.description:
At most 16,777,216 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `request_body_too_large` before JSON parsing. Created resources belong to the authenticated account. Submitted owner identities cannot assign or transfer ownership. Standalone run records and subject histories are private to their initiating account, including for administrators. Standalone jobs retain their initiating owner before any output exists, after failure and after output deletion; contained jobs follow their workflow, read by everyone who reaches it and cancelled by their initiator or the workflow's owner. Unreached and missing run identities return not_found before cancellation or private content reads. Subject grouping, history pruning and output-name conflicts are account-local. Workers recheck account activity before preparation and at publication; an inactive owner's unfinished job fails with authentication_required and keeps no new output, and an input another account owns that is no longer within the runner's reach when the output commits refuses it with sql_error naming the input as written. Accepts one operation and answers **202** with a run, before the work is done; poll the run's own resource for its outcome. An accepted run outlives the request that started it. Closing the connection does not stop it.

What is refused here, and what is reported on the run, is a fixed line. Refused immediately, minting no run: a malformed body, an unknown operation, SQL that is not an accepted read-only SELECT, an output name already taken, and a full queue. Reported on the run instead: SQL that parses but fails to bind or execute, a name taken between acceptance and commit, the engine memory budget, the execution budget, and a server stopped mid-run.

Set dryRun to ask what the operation would produce without writing anything; a dry run is synchronous and mints no run.

A parameter that names a dataset takes the caller's own dataset by its bare name, and another person's dataset the caller reaches by its qualified name, <sql name>.<name>; a dataset out of reach is refused exactly as one that does not exist.

Give `writtenIn` when the parameters were written in a map's home or a workflow (a result previewed there and saved as a dataset, a tool previewing a layer's SQL): they are carried into the caller's own console, where a run reads its names, and the output is the caller's own dataset either way. Each dataset reference keeps the dataset it meant where it was written: a plain name of a dataset the destination's SQL home does not own, or whose name an output there takes, becomes <sql name>.<dataset>; an already qualified name stays as written; a workflow's own output becomes the dataset the caller's latest successful run of it made. Only those references change; the rest of the text is kept as written, and nothing where it came from is touched. A reference that cannot be carried (a dataset outside the caller's reach, an output the caller has not produced, a computed table name that would have to change) refuses the request with sql_error naming it, and nothing is written.

Only one read-only SELECT over named datasets is accepted. File readers, file-relation shorthand and engine path or definition discovery are refused before binding with sql_rejected, including nested SQL and computed targets. File-referencing PROJ coordinate definitions are also refused before native projection use, including computed or per-row values; EPSG identifiers and inline definitions without files remain supported. Unknown tables receive the same sql_error whether hidden or nonexistent, without catalogue suggestions. Engine errors do not expose filesystem paths or internal statements; input positions are retained when available. Existing saved SQL is retained unchanged; affected saved and published queries fail. **sql_step** keeps the result of a read-only SELECT as a dataset: the escape hatch inside any recipe, and the way to save a query you already trust. A result with no geometry is an ordinary dataset, not a failure.

**Measurements are ground metres.** A buffer's radius and a measured length are metres on the earth, at the latitude the data occupies, never degrees or metres on a map projection. They are measured in a transverse Mercator centred on the data's own extent, every input counted, and the output's provenance records it. Data too wide for that to hold within 1 % everywhere, or crossing the antimeridian, is **refused** for a distance with `measurement_crs_unavailable`, naming its width and extent; an **area** over the same data succeeds, because every area is measured in a global equal-area projection. An input whose coordinate system was assumed rather than declared is measured anyway and the answer says so, on the dry run, on the accepted run, and on the output.

operation.description: An operation id from the catalog.

parameters.description: The operation's own parameters, as the catalog describes them.

subject.description: Groups this run with others in history, so 'when did this last succeed' has an answer across re-runs. Omitted, the run is its own subject.

dryRun.description: Report what the run would produce and write nothing.

writtenIn.description: Where `parameters` were written, when not the caller's own console; they are carried into it.

get.description: A workflow is reached by its owner and, while it is filed in a project, by that project's owner and people; its steps, layout and runs follow it. Results name the workflow's owner and SQL home and are read in that home within the caller's own reach: a reference the caller cannot reach is missing to them, named as written, and recorded lineage, output links and captured layer identities out of their reach are left out. Content changes are open to the owner, the project's owner and its editors; the SQL and dataset parameters anyone but the owner saves into a step must name only datasets within their own reach in the workflow's home, the workflow's declared outputs aside, else the save is refused with sql_error naming the reference as written and nothing changes. Deletion stays the owner's. Anyone who reaches a workflow may duplicate it into their own space: the copy keeps the workflow's SQL home and is filed in its project only when the duplicator may file there (its owner or an editor). Administrators reach nothing more. Unreached or missing workflows, steps, captured layers and project references return not_found before reading private contents or changing resources; a reached workflow whose change the caller may not make returns forbidden and changes nothing. A step's declared output name is taken when a dataset of that name is in the workflow's SQL home or in the declaring person's own space, and duplicate-name allocation considers the duplicator's own datasets and workflows and the datasets of the SQL home the copy keeps, both preserving the existing same-workflow conflict rules. Accepted changes recheck account activity and referenced-resource access at commit. Every recipe the caller reaches (their own, and every one filed in a project they own or belong to), each with its steps and their current conditions, what each step reads now, and a summary of the whole (its status and counts). A recipe is a workspace object like a dataset — not owned by a map, and outliving the layer that prompted it. `origin` narrows the answer to the workflows page's own (`workflow`) or the builder's one-step recipes (`builder`); unfiltered, both answer.

Appends a step naming an operation from the catalog, its parameters, and the dataset it will produce.

**The output's name**: stored in the registry's form; a blank or letterless name is refused in its own words; a name a registered table carries, or another step of this recipe declares or holds, is refused (`name_taken`) naming the holder. Another recipe's unrun declaration is no reservation. A step may be added unnamed; the run refuses a nameless one. **SQL the parser cannot read is accepted** with no present reads; the dry run and the run refuse it and say why.

Give `fromLayerId` to author it from a layer: the step takes that layer's SQL **refined by its filters**, captured now and never re-read, so the step stays reproducible when the filters later change. Where the layer is drawn as hex bins, grid cells or origin–destination lines, the step consumes the **rows behind** those cells rather than the cells themselves, and the answer says so in `origin.substitutionNote`. Any layer the caller reaches can be captured, its SQL carried from its map's home into this workflow's context; one the caller does not reach answers as a missing one.

Give `writtenIn` when the parameters were written elsewhere (a node copied from another workflow, the caller's console, a map): their dataset inputs and SQL are carried into this workflow's context, where this step's own output already takes its name. Each dataset reference keeps the dataset it meant where it was written: a plain name of a dataset the destination's SQL home does not own, or whose name an output there takes, becomes <sql name>.<dataset>; an already qualified name stays as written; a workflow's own output becomes the dataset the caller's latest successful run of it made. Only those references change; the rest of the text is kept as written, and nothing where it came from is touched. A reference that cannot be carried (a dataset outside the caller's reach, an output the caller has not produced, a computed table name that would have to change) refuses the request with sql_error naming it, and nothing is written.

A step that would read its own output, or a later step's, is refused here rather than at run time.

post.description:
Created resources belong to the authenticated account. Submitted owner identities cannot assign or transfer ownership. Workflow runs, member attempts and retained outputs follow their workflow: everyone who reaches it reads its runs, with output links out of the caller's reach left out. Planning and starting a run are open to whoever may change the workflow's content (its owner, the project's owner and its editors); a viewer is refused with forbidden before anything is planned. A run is its runner's: it reads in the workflow's SQL home within the runner's reach, its outputs are created as the runner's own datasets, never replacing anyone else's, and are filed into the workflow's project as it stands when each output commits, when the runner may file there; a rerun replaces only the same runner's earlier output of that step, and a dataset of the runner's already holding the name is refused with name_taken. A run is cancelled by its initiator or the workflow's owner; an initiator who no longer reaches the workflow still cancels their own run by its identifier, answered 204 without the run. Administrators reach nothing more. Every referenced step and run must belong to the addressed workflow; unreached, missing and mixed-parent references return not_found before planning or execution. Account activity is checked after planning, at worker entry and at publication. At each output's commit the runner's permission and reach to every input are checked again: an input another account owns that the runner no longer reaches refuses that output with sql_error naming it as written, even though the step already read it; a runner who may no longer run the workflow (no longer its editor, or no longer reaching it after it was unfiled, moved, dissolved out of its project or transferred) completes the steps already admitted privately, into their own datasets, unfiled, leaving the workflow's recorded outputs, proposals and definitions unchanged, and no further step is admitted; the run records each outcome. A workflow moved or transferred while running files each output into its project as it stands at commit. Deactivation prevents further admission and publication, drains admitted work and retains already committed outputs and terminal attempts. Results remain owned after step or output deletion and independent job-history pruning. Restart marks unfinished runs interrupted without executing them again. Answers **202** with one of the recipe's runs: a run of kind `single` with this one member, listed among the recipe's runs and read and cancelled through them; poll `/api/recipes/{id}/runs/{runId}` for its outcome. **This runs the step and nothing else** — carrying its dependents is the recipe-run endpoint's job.

Ordinary maximum-shape layout documents fit; escape-inflated keys and unbounded note ids can exceed the outer byte bound and are refused by design.

Omit `fromStepId` to run the whole recipe from the beginning; give one to re-run that step and everything that reads it, in dependency order. A step starts only once every step it reads has succeeded, and one whose dependency failed is **not attempted** — reported `not_run`, minting no run at all, with the failure that stopped it named. Steps that do not depend on the failure still run.

**Ask first with `plan: true`.** It answers what the request would carry and the editRevision paired with that definition, without starting anything. Starting requires that revision in X-Edit-Revision, including when planning awaits asynchronous work. A changed basis refuses with stale_revision before any run or output exists. `wide` is true for a run of the whole recipe and for a re-run that carries dependents, and false for the same request aimed at a step nothing reads. That is what the `when_wide` confirmation on this operation means — confirm the wide cases, not the leaf.

A recipe run is **not** an operation run: it answers **202** with its own resource, which has its own outcome and contains the members' ordinary runs.

**What a caller may rely on.** A recipe runs one run at a time: a start while one is in flight — this operation's or a single step's — answers **409 `run_in_flight`** naming the run, and two starts that race yield one run and one refusal. A start that names `members` — the step ids a confirmation listed, in order — starts exactly when the plan at start is that set in that order, and answers **409 `plan_changed`** otherwise, nothing started. This membership check accompanies the start revision check. Each member is read when admitted. Each attempted member's record carries its attempt — state, error, times, output — kept with the run after the step's own history is pruned; a member never attempted has none; every member keeps its step's operation and name after the step is removed.

get.description: A map is reached by its owner and, while it is filed in a project, by that project's owner and people. Results cover exactly the reached maps and name each map's owner and SQL home; the map's SQL is evaluated in its home within the caller's own reach. Content changes are open to the owner, the project's owner and its editors; SQL anyone but the owner saves, directly or by undo and redo, must name only datasets within their own reach in the map's home, else it is refused with sql_error naming the reference as written and nothing changes. Sketches drawn on the map are content, each sketch dataset its drawer's own; deletion and publication settings stay the owner's; the server makes pictures as the owner, and an Editor may request a refresh; a snapshot is served to everyone who reaches the map and every dataset it drew. Anyone who reaches a map may duplicate it into their own space: the copy keeps the map's SQL home and its layers' SQL as stored, is filed in the map's project only when the duplicator may file there (its owner or an editor), and carries the snapshot only when the duplicator may be served it. Administrators reach nothing more. Unreached and missing map or project identities both return not_found before source access or protected changes; a reached map whose change the caller may not make returns forbidden and changes nothing.

post.summary: Export a project as one archive
post.description: At most 16,777,216 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `request_body_too_large` before JSON parsing. Private execution retains the initiating account through completion. Retained images and download receipts belong only to that account, including for administrators, even after the source or output is deleted. A copied result identifier has the same refusal as an unknown identifier and cannot consume or release the owner's result. Account activity is checked before returning bytes or retaining a new result; deactivation freezes access until reactivation. Reach is asked again where the work commits. A prepared layer download is refused on the claim when its layer, on a map the claimant does not own, or a dataset it drew that someone else owns has left the claimant's reach since the ticket, with the same answer as an expired ticket. A server render and a look check ask at every phase whether the caller still reaches the map and are refused as absent otherwise. A project export checks every selected member against the caller's reach as the archive completes and fails with export_failed naming the first one withdrawn rather than delivering a thinner archive. Results already issued (a query download, a retained look image, a project archive, an assistant answer) remain the initiator's for their retention lifetime after reach is withdrawn, as a copy they hold; they grant no new access to the source. A project is reached by its owner and by its people, its viewers and editors. Lists, counts and member lists cover exactly the reached projects and everything filed in them, whoever owns it, and name each project's owner and the caller's role (owner, editor or viewer). Renaming, the note, dissolution, adding people, changing their roles, removing other people and its transfer are the owner's; a member may leave their own grant, including in a frozen project; administrators reach nothing more. Filing follows its own rules: adding a map, workflow or dataset needs the destination's permission (the project's owner, or an editor filing their own resource) and a project whose owner is active; the owner of a resource may always withdraw it from any project, member or not; the project's owner may remove anything filed in their project, which never deletes it or changes its owner. Unreached or missing references return the same not_found before changes or archive assembly; a reached project whose change the caller may not make returns forbidden and changes nothing. Compound changes are atomic. Deleting a project unfiles its contents without deleting artifacts or changing their owners. Anyone who reaches a project may export it, viewers included: a selection names members filed in it that the caller reaches, whoever owns them. A chosen subset of the project's members as one zip: datasets byte for byte as their stored GeoParquet artifacts — or, with datasetFormat, every dataset converted to GeoJSON or CSV, a dataset without geometry going as CSV under GeoJSON and the manifest naming each dataset's effective format — maps and workflows (workflow-origin recipes) as portable JSON projections (publication state, membership and runtime stripped; the workflow carries its canvas layout), and a versioned project.json manifest naming every included member. Every dataset has its own entry under the name the exporter types for it, its qualifiedName: the plain name for the exporter's own, <sql name>.<name> for another owner's, so two people's same-named datasets never collide; the manifest names each one's qualifiedName and owner and the exporter's SQL name (exportedBy). Map and workflow documents carry their SQL home, the account whose datasets their plain names mean. No connection facts travel. The archive is assembled and finalized before any success is claimed — a failed assembly is a coded refusal, never a truncated file. Refuses an unknown project, an empty selection, and any id that is not a current member. The response is an attachment named <file>.zip; through the agent tool it arrives as a base64 attachment envelope. With prepare, a single-use ticket instead — the page's road; redeem it with GET within a minute.

prepare.description: Answer a single-use ticket {ticket, key, filename, size} instead of the bytes.

datasetFormat.description: One format for every dataset in the archive. Omitted or geoparquet: the stored artifact byte for byte. geojson: spatial datasets as GeoJSON, a dataset without geometry as CSV. csv: geometry as WKT text. The manifest records each dataset's effective format beside its file; the format version stays 1.

200.description: The zip attachment — or, with prepare, the JSON ticket.

Renaming, the note, dissolution, adding people, changing their roles, removing other people and its transfer are the owner's; a member may leave their own grant, including in a frozen project; administrators reach nothing more. Filing follows its own rules: adding a map, workflow or dataset needs the destination's permission (the project's owner, or an editor filing their own resource) and a project whose owner is active; the owner of a resource may always withdraw it from any project, member or not; the project's owner may remove anything filed in their project, which never deletes it or changes its owner. Unreached or missing references return the same not_found before changes or archive assembly; a reached project whose change the caller may not make returns forbidden and changes nothing. Compound changes are atomic. Deleting a project unfiles its contents without deleting artifacts or changing their owners. Anyone who reaches a project may export it, viewers included: a selection names members filed in it that the caller reaches, whoever owns them. An active viewer or editor may leave, including a frozen project. The credential supplies the departing member; there is no request body or member selector. Ends only that member's grant, with exactly the same reach loss as removal by the owner: exclusive reach ends on the next request, and the project disappears from lists and filters on the next read. Other grants and ownership remain. Owned work stays filed and shared, readable by its owner with the project's identity for withdrawal. Historical attribution stays named. Already admitted reads finish once; outputs recheck permission and input reach at commit, as after removal. Membership changes no edit revisions. No consent or notification is required, and the owner may add the person again normally. Answers only departure, never a roster. Missing and non-member projects both answer 404 not_found; owners answer 409 project_owner_cannot_leave. A repeated departure answers not_found.

post.description: At most 16,777,216 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `request_body_too_large` before JSON parsing. A map is reached by its owner and, while it is filed in a project, by that project's owner and people. Content changes are open to the owner, the project's owner and its editors; SQL anyone but the owner saves, directly or by undo and redo, must name only datasets within their own reach in the map's home, else it is refused with sql_error naming the reference as written and nothing changes. Sketches drawn on the map are content, each sketch dataset its drawer's own; deletion and publication settings stay the owner's; the server makes pictures as the owner, and an Editor may request a refresh; a snapshot is served to everyone who reaches the map and every dataset it drew. Anyone who reaches a map may duplicate it into their own space: the copy keeps the map's SQL home and its layers' SQL as stored, is filed in the map's project only when the duplicator may file there (its owner or an editor), and carries the snapshot only when the duplicator may be served it. Transfer is the only change of ownership any operation makes, and it is always the current owner's own act. The new owner is named by their SQL name and must be an active account. Makes another active person who already reaches the map its owner: the owner of the project it is filed in, or one of that project's people. An unfiled map is refused with invalid_request: file the map in a project first. The map keeps its SQL home, so its SQL means what it meant, and it keeps its layers, history, card images and its publication, which becomes the new owner's and renders with the new owner's reach: a dataset the new owner cannot reach fails on the link rather than drawing anything else. Anyone who reaches a map may duplicate it into their own space: the copy keeps the map's SQL home and its layers' SQL as stored, is filed in the map's project only when the duplicator may file there (its owner or an editor), and carries the snapshot only when the duplicator may be served it. Administrators reach nothing more. Unreached and missing map or project identities both return not_found before source access or protected changes; a reached map whose change the caller may not make returns forbidden and changes nothing.

post.summary: Look at a map: one bounded rendered image with its facts
post.description: At most 16,777,216 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `request_body_too_large` before JSON parsing. Requires a current cookie session or bearer token. Cookie mutations require the same trusted Origin. Responses, including refusals, are private, no-store. Private execution retains the initiating account through completion. Retained images and download receipts belong only to that account, including for administrators, even after the source or output is deleted. A copied result identifier has the same refusal as an unknown identifier and cannot consume or release the owner's result. Account activity is checked before returning bytes or retaining a new result; deactivation freezes access until reactivation. Reach is asked again where the work commits. A prepared layer download is refused on the claim when its layer, on a map the claimant does not own, or a dataset it drew that someone else owns has left the claimant's reach since the ticket, with the same answer as an expired ticket. A server render and a look check ask at every phase whether the caller still reaches the map and are refused as absent otherwise. A project export checks every selected member against the caller's reach as the archive completes and fails with export_failed naming the first one withdrawn rather than delivering a thinner archive. Results already issued (a query download, a retained look image, a project archive, an assistant answer) remain the initiator's for their retention lifetime after reach is withdrawn, as a copy they hold; they grant no new access to the source. A map is reached by its owner and, while it is filed in a project, by that project's owner and people. Results cover exactly the reached maps and name each map's owner and SQL home; the map's SQL is evaluated in its home within the caller's own reach. Content changes are open to the owner, the project's owner and its editors; SQL anyone but the owner saves, directly or by undo and redo, must name only datasets within their own reach in the map's home, else it is refused with sql_error naming the reference as written and nothing changes. Sketches drawn on the map are content, each sketch dataset its drawer's own; deletion and publication settings stay the owner's; the server makes pictures as the owner, and an Editor may request a refresh; a snapshot is served to everyone who reaches the map and every dataset it drew. Anyone who reaches a map may duplicate it into their own space: the copy keeps the map's SQL home and its layers' SQL as stored, is filed in the map's project only when the duplicator may file there (its owner or an editor), and carries the snapshot only when the duplicator may be served it. Administrators reach nothing more. Unreached and missing map or project identities both return not_found before source access or protected changes; a reached map whose change the caller may not make returns forbidden and changes nothing. The model-facing check of a map: the map's stored state rendered through the same server-side road as the image export, at 1024 by 640 pixels, and answered as a PNG of at most 384 KiB together with the render's facts. The image is derived from that one render downwards through 768 by 480 and 512 by 320 when the byte bound is missed; still over it at 512 by 320 the answer is look_image_too_large and no image. The facts carry the render's identity, the bounded state identity of what the renderer actually drew (the map, the camera, the visible layers with a digest of their stored filters, the legend and the widgets, the appearance), the image's pixel and byte sizes, the source size, the attribution credited, the composition's truthful failures and any abandoned external requests, and the elapsed time. The appearance is an explicit input, light when absent; mapId names the map, and a call naming none answers look_target_missing. Read-only: the map's stored state stays as it is; the image is retained in process for GET /api/maps/look/{renderId} under documented bounds. Bounded by its own budget (30 s by default, DEZFIL_ASSISTANT_LOOK_TIMEOUT_S), queue wait, render and image preparation included; past it the answer is render_timeout. Without a renderer browser on the instance the answer is render_unavailable.

get.description: Render results follow the layer's map: everyone who reaches it reads them, evaluated in the map's SQL home within their own reach. Tile archives record the datasets they drew and are served to a caller only while that caller can reach every one of them; administrators reach nothing more. An archive made before archives recorded their inputs is served to the map's owner alone. Builds are kept apart by the reach that asked for them: a refused or failed build is that reach's alone, reported as failed to it for the same query, and never replaces the archive or the status anyone else is served. Unreached and missing layers return the same not_found before archive reads or build admission. Private tile workers recheck account activity before export and on both sides of archive publication; deactivation leaves no new authoritative archive. Private reads recheck authority before answering. Deleting an owned layer fences its outstanding build. Reactivation permits a fresh build. A visible published layer uses its current token independently of the publisher's activity; a revoked token cannot authorize a new archive. Layers and widgets follow their map: everyone who reaches the map reads and evaluates them, and its owner, the project's owner and its editors change them. Layer SQL saved by anyone but the map's owner must name only datasets within their own reach in the map's home, else it is refused with sql_error naming the reference as written and nothing changes. Unreached, missing or mismatched parent/child identities return not_found before query evaluation, artifact access or protected changes. New widget, timeline and layer-order references must belong to the exact map. The layer's effective result — its SQL refined by its filters, then aggregated by its viz (hexbin/grid cells expose value and count). Under the render cap the response is inline GeoJSON (mode: inline). A points-viz result over the cap is served as vector tiles instead (mode: tiled): tiles are prepared in the background — poll while `tiles.state` is `building`; when `ready`, `tiles.url` is a {z}/{x}/{y} template and bounds/zoom range describe the archive. Inline feature properties are the columns the layer and its map read: its style, label and label-priority fields, the filters the canvas applies, the docked timeline's field, the fields of the map's widgets on it, its explicit tooltip and pop-up fields or, while either list is automatic, the first eight columns, and a drawn sketch's feature_id and kind; other columns stay out, and the published field list plays no part. The inline answer, envelope included, is bounded by Bytes drawn per layer (renderCapBytes), counted as it is built. Above it the layer takes the road it takes over the cap: a points-viz result is served as tiles, a result shipped without its live filters has them applied in the query and is answered inline if that fits, and anything else answers the errored state render_bytes_exceeded. A template's layer has no tile road. Errored states (deleted table, failed build, missing tiler, an aggregation over the cap, an answer over the byte limit) are returned as data, not an HTTP error.

On dataset reads, features, downloads and operation parameters, another owner's dataset the caller reaches is addressed by its qualified name, and in a /api/tables path also by its identifier; changing one by any address answers forbidden. Unreached and missing datasets, maps and project references return not_found before source or artifact access; a refused change leaves resources unchanged. Refresh and geometry changes preserve the dataset's identity and owner and recheck account activity at commit. Names, stable identities, owners, the reached projects each dataset is filed in, recorded row counts and geometry facts with stored artifact column names and types. Reads metadata only, without evaluating row previews or healing geometry records. Recorded geometry identity is separate from the physical column type. Ordered by qualifiedName, the name the caller would type, which is unique within the caller's reach: two same-named datasets of different owners each appear exactly once. At most 32 tables and 64 columns per table per page. after continues tables; columnOffset continues columns for a named table. total counts matching tables, columnCount counts each table’s columns. Incomplete collections carry nextAfter or nextColumnOffset. A missing artifact fails the read instead of returning a false empty schema. Responses are bounded to 96 KiB; a response that cannot fit answers 422 catalogue_too_large so the caller can request fewer tables or columns. No artifact paths, source configuration, credentials, row samples or attachment bytes are returned.

post.summary: Send a message to the assistant
post.description: At most 131,072 wire bytes; a larger body is refused with `assistant_submission_too_large` before JSON parsing. Requires a current cookie session or bearer token. Cookie mutations require the same trusted Origin. Responses, including refusals, are private, no-store. Reservations and pending actions are bound to their account. Every continuation reauthenticates that same account and uses its current permissions. A foreign run is unavailable; a foreign pending action is unknown. Grounding, subject reads, execution and automatic checks use the caller’s bearer-equivalent identity on every internal request. No credential is retained with a pending action. Every new message requires a runId from POST /api/assistant/runs. Unreserved requests refuse with 400 assistant_reservation_required before work. Unknown or evicted identities refuse with 404 assistant_run_unavailable. The first accepted submission binds its message, history, context and supersession. Identical concurrent or later submissions return an application/json AssistantRun snapshot without another exchange; changed input refuses with 409 assistant_run_conflict. Plain-English request; the assistant works through the same documented API these docs describe and streams its actions back as newline-delimited JSON events (application/x-ndjson): assistant text, tool calls and their results, confirmation prompts for destructive or publishing actions, and a terminal done/error. A confirm_required event pauses the run and carries a server-issued pending-action id; resolve it by posting a resolution referencing that id. Approval executes exactly the presented action once and the run continues where it paused, a decline skips it and the assistant finishes its turn. A pending action resolves at most once (409 pending_resolved on a repeat); a new message may name a pending action it supersedes (the implicit decline), after which resolution answers 409 pending_superseded. A hidden or unknown pending id cannot be resolved; naming one only to supersede it is a harmless no-op. Pending actions are working state, and bounded: after a container replacement resolution answers 404 pending_unknown and nothing re-runs; only a small number of reserved, running or parked runs share eight admission slots. A full instance refuses new reservations with assistant_capacity; live and pending runs are never silently evicted. Only unused reservations expire after five minutes. Pending turns have no wall-clock expiry and are recoverable through GET /api/assistant/pending. Release a reservation or abandon a pending turn with DELETE /api/assistant/runs/{id}. The resolved trace behind the 409 answers is bounded, so a sufficiently old repeat answers pending_unknown instead. The step budget spans the whole turn, pauses included. Submissions above 128 KiB refuse with assistant_submission_too_large before work. Terminal recovery keeps 256 receipts of at most 64 KiB; live recovery is at most 1 MiB per run and stops with assistant_recovery_limit before protected action data would exceed it. Returns 404 with assistant_disabled when no model credential is configured. The page action policy binds at the first accepted submission from the context's page and holds through the run's confirmation continuations: a builder context, and no context, admit every generated tool with its confirmation gates; a sql context and a workflow context admit only the operations that declare themselves read-only by their effects, the read-only query and the schema reads among them, and no operation that declares a write on any argument, conditional (plan or run) operations included; of the read-only ones they refuse any that reaches outside this server or asks for confirmation, a service's or a part's Test among them. The model is offered only what its run admits. A call outside the set, however it arrives, is refused before any product operation: its tool_result carries the documented error assistant_action_not_admitted and the run's receipt records the action as refused. A message may carry an optional choice of model and effort; GET /api/assistant reports what this instance offers. It binds with the rest of the submission at the first accepted one and holds through every continuation of the run; a choice on a resolution is ignored. A malformed choice, a model this instance does not offer, an effort the selected model does not offer and a named level for a model that has no levels of its own refuse with 400 assistant_choice_invalid, assistant_model_not_offered, assistant_effort_not_offered and assistant_effort_not_supported respectively, each before the run binds and before any provider call or product operation, leaving the reservation unbound and reusable. The run's receipt reports the pair it bound and, separately, the identities its completed provider responses named.

get.summary: One imagery tile of a published map
get.description: Verified ingress source is charged before token resolution, including unknown tokens. The five view operations, the satellite style among them, share one source budget across tokens (default 60 per ten seconds); tiles, the satellite tiles among them, have a separate budget (default 600). Missing or forged provenance answers 503 ingress_unavailable. The combined state holds at most 10,000 entries, expired on traffic then evicted least recently used; eviction grants a fresh window. Untrusted proxies share their socket budget. Every address of one IPv6 /64 is charged to one budget; an IPv4 source is charged alone, whether mapped, reaching the instance through the NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96, or neither. The token evaluates the map's SQL in its SQL home with the map owner's current reach, independently of visitor credentials, including while the owner is deactivated, restricted to the datasets the map's own layers name: nothing else of the owner's space is mounted for the link. A layer or widget that reads the instance's catalogue fails with catalogue_not_published while the owner holds datasets the map does not name, and one naming a dataset the owner can no longer reach fails with sql_error. Before first-account setup, a legacy token has only its pending-adoption publication scope; setup retires that scope atomically. Revocation is checked after asynchronous work before returning results. The projection never exposes account identity, private SQL, dataset paths or connection credentials. Fetched now by the server from the tile template this instance configures and passed back, so the template and a key in it never leave the server. Use the tile address the imagery style names. Only the tile's z, x and y reach the template, each a whole number in plain decimal, z from 0 to 19 and x and y below 2 to the power of z, the row followed by @2x for a high-density tile or by nothing; anything else is refused with invalid_request before the imagery is asked. The template is filled from these alone as MapLibre fills a raster template: {z}, {x}, {y} (counted by the style source's scheme), {ratio} (@2x or nothing), {quadkey}, {prefix} and {bbox-epsg-3857}. No query, header or credential of the request goes with them. The fetch takes the egress policy at every hop, waits at most ten seconds and reads at most 4 MiB; only a whole PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or AVIF image passes back, with the type its bytes are, and no tile is stored. Every failure upstream answers imagery_unavailable, whose message says what went wrong and never the tile address or its key; a template carrying a user name or password is not drawn and answers the same. Private, no-store. In the tile budget. Served under the publish token only while the publication resolves, as its layer tiles are: a revoked or unknown token answers the same clean not_found, and so does a publication whose reader is not shown Satellite (the map is not on it, and its basemap switcher is off or no longer offers it). An instance with no imagery to draw now, none configured or a stored template its key no longer opens, answers 404 as the signed-in style does while none is configured. The token is checked again once the tile has come, so a publication revoked meanwhile passes nothing back.
