CookieSession.name: dezfil_session
CookieSession.description: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session. Secure over HTTPS. On a listening port other than 3000 the name carries the port suffix, and DEZFIL_SESSION_COOKIE sets the name. Lasts the instance's session length, security.sessionDays, thirty days by default; each use renews it by the length stored then. Optional X-Dezfil-Account asserts the credential's expected account ID. A mismatch returns 401 authentication_required before dispatch. This transport precondition never supplies identity or changes ownership.

BearerToken.description: An account's API token. Its current account status and privileges are checked on every request; once a token's expiry passes it is refused with token_expired. Optional X-Dezfil-Account asserts the credential's expected account ID. A mismatch returns 401 authentication_required before dispatch. This transport precondition never supplies identity or changes ownership.

sqlName.description: The account's SQL name, unique on the instance. Derived from the display name (else the email's local part, else the word user, with a number added on a collision or a name the query engine reserves) when the account is created or upgraded, and fixed thereafter: changing the name or email never changes it.

pictureVersion.description: The version of the person's picture, present while they have one and new whenever it is replaced; absent while they have none, when their initials stand in. GET /api/accounts/{sqlName}/picture?v=<version> reads it.

passwordMin.description: The fewest characters a password chosen on these screens needs: 8 for the first account, then the instance's shortest password, which admins set from 8 to 64.

Person.description: A person a resource names where the app draws their face, such as its owner. The display name, the SQL name and the picture's version, never an email.

sqlName.description: The person's SQL name, the qualifier other people's SQL uses for their datasets.

pictureVersion.description: The version of the person's picture, present while they have one and new whenever it is replaced; absent while they have none, when their initials stand in. GET /api/accounts/{sqlName}/picture?v=<version> reads it.

A map or workflow the caller does not reach answers as a missing one.

id.description: The map or workflow; absent for console.

expiresAt.description: When the token stops working; null when it never expires. An expired token is refused with token_expired and stays listed until revoked.

s3Endpoint.description: S3 endpoint. The S3-compatible store that s3:// links are read from without the server's credentials. Null clears the stored value. An http or https address with a host, at most 2048 characters once trimmed, kept as given. Write-only: it is stored encrypted with the instance's key and every read gives back its scheme and host alone, so a new key means sending the whole address again. A set DEZFIL_S3_ENDPOINT locks it.

overpassUrl.description: Overpass endpoint. Endpoint for OpenStreetMap imports. Null clears the stored value. An http or https address with a host, at most 2048 characters once trimmed, kept as given. Write-only: it is stored encrypted with the instance's key and every read gives back its scheme and host alone, so a new key means sending the whole address again. A set DEZFIL_OVERPASS_URL locks it.

satelliteUrl.description: Satellite template. Raster tile template enabling satellite imagery. Null clears the stored value. An http or https address with a host, at most 2048 characters once trimmed, kept as given. It must hold {z}, {x}, {y}; the save-time check reads it with each filled with a digit. It must carry no user name or password: the imagery is not drawn from such an address, so the key belongs in the path or the query. Write-only: it is stored encrypted with the instance's key and every read gives back its scheme and host alone, so a new key means sending the whole address again. A set DEZFIL_SATELLITE_URL locks it.

satelliteAttribution.description: Satellite credit. Credit line required by the imagery provider. Null clears the stored value. Text is trimmed before the 160-character limit; empty text clears to the default. A set DEZFIL_SATELLITE_ATTRIBUTION locks it.

geocoderUrl.description: Address finder. Nominatim-compatible endpoint for search and batch geocoding. Null clears the stored value. Write-only: it is stored encrypted with the instance's key and every read gives back its scheme and host alone, so a new key means sending the whole address again. A set DEZFIL_GEOCODER_URL locks it.

isochroneUrl.description: Travel-time endpoint. Valhalla-compatible endpoint for travel-time areas. Null clears the stored value. errorCode.description: One of the documented error codes.

coordinates.description: Every plausible reading of a pasted decimal pair — both when both are valid.

places.description: The places group's answer: `ok` with results and the provider's attribution, `unconfigured`, or `failed` with a sanitized message (never the provider URL).

OperationCatalog.description: The verbs this instance offers, as data. An agent discovers what it may ask the run endpoint for by reading this rather than by knowing the verbs in advance — which is why every field a caller needs in order to build a legal request is declared here.

symbol.description: Glyph name a picker draws beside the label — presentation metadata, stable per verb, from the app's shared icon set.

blurb.description: One plain-text line for pickers. `description` is the reference text; this is the working surface's sentence.

inputs.description: The datasets this verb takes and what each is for. A verb with two inputs has two that are not interchangeable — a spatial join's left and right mean different things, and the output's geometry comes from one of them. A verb that declares none takes its input from whatever its own SQL names, which is a different thing from taking no input at all.

accepts.description: Geometry classes this particular input accepts. "none" is the opposite of "any": it admits only a table without geometry, which is what a verb that writes a geometry column onto every row takes.
Input geometry classes the operation accepts overall; "any" includes a table with no geometry, and "none" admits only one.

requires.description: What this instance must be configured with for the verb to run at all. A verb that declares none always runs.

availability.description: Whether *this* instance can run the verb, resolved when the catalog is served rather than declared — an operator who configures a provider changes the answer without changing a verb. A verb with no requirement answers available.

reason.description: Why not, when it cannot — one sentence a reader can act on, naming the setting that is missing.

outputGeometry.description: Where the result's geometry comes from. A verb that fixes its class regardless of input declares it; one that passes geometry through names the input it comes from; one whose result must be inspected says so.

min.description: Hard lower bound, where the verb has one.

max.description: Hard upper bound, where the verb has one.

type.description: `enum` is one value from `options`; `enum_list` is several, as a list. They are distinct because a caller told `enum` where a list is required has been given the wrong shape. `field` is one column of the named input; `column_list` is several columns, as names; `field_list` is several **aggregate specifications** — `{aggregate, field, as}` — and sending one shape where the other is expected is refused.

options.description: The permitted values for an enum or enum list, fixed by the operation's own contract rather than by whatever the engine happens to offer. On a `field_list` these are the aggregates that parameter accepts, which differ between verbs.

aliasable.description: Whether a carried value may be given a name of its own. A summary's aggregates cannot, and an editor offering the field would produce a name the operation ignores.

requiredWhen.description: What makes this parameter required, when it is not always — a distance is needed only for a within-distance relationship. Declared so a caller knows before it sends rather than after the refusal.

relevantWhen.description: When this parameter is part of the question at all — absent means always; present, it only applies while the named parameter holds one of these values. A distance is no part of an "intersects" question. Distinct from requiredWhen: a parameter can be used without being required. A value sent for an inapplicable parameter is ignored or refused by the operation's own admission, so callers should omit it.

ofInput.description: Which input a field parameter names a column of.

fieldType.description: The kind of column a field parameter may name, when the verb needs one kind. Declared so a caller offers or sends a column that can work rather than learning from a refusal; admission checks the same rule.

minItems.description: For a number_list: the fewest items the list takes.

maxItems.description: For a number_list: the most items the list takes — the isochrone's four bands is the protocol's own maximum.

itemMin.description: For a number_list: the floor every item must clear.

itemInteger.description: For a number_list: items must be whole numbers.

itemsUnique.description: For a number_list: duplicate items are refused — each band is asked once.

unit.description: Present when the value is not a bare number: `metres` is a **ground measurement** — metres on the earth, at the latitude the data occupies, never degrees and never metres on a map projection; a caller that ignores this and sends the geometry's own units gets a buffer five hundred degrees wide. `minutes` is travel time: the number the user typed is the number on the wire, no conversion exists.

default.description: The value used when the parameter is omitted.

OperationMeasurement.description: Where a run measured. A buffer whose record does not name its measurement CRS is not reproducible — the same operation with the same parameters can produce a different geometry under a later strategy, and nothing would explain the difference.

crs.description: The CRS each kind of measurement happened in, keyed by kind. A distance is measured in a transverse Mercator centred on the data's own extent, recorded as its PROJ definition; an area in a global equal-area projection, recorded as its EPSG code.

fallback.description: True when a measurement was made in a global projection rather than a local one, so a number measured globally is never read back as one measured locally.

assumedCrs.description: Inputs whose WGS84 was assumed rather than declared. The measurement is only as trustworthy as that assumption.

OperationDryRun.description: The answer to dryRun: what the operation would produce, with nothing written.

warnings.description: Non-fatal facts to read before committing to the run — today, that a measured input's coordinate system was assumed rather than declared. Said here so a caller learns it *before* running, not after.

geometryType.description: The class the registered dataset would carry, in the same words an imported table holding that geometry does.

geometry.description: Which of the three answers this is. 'none' — the result has no geometry column and would be a table, not a mappable layer. 'undetermined' — it has one but no geometries to classify. 'classified' — geometryType names its class. A null geometryType alone cannot tell the first two apart.

OperationRun.description:
One run of an operation. The same shape in every state, so a queued run and a finished one are read the same way.

Fields that have not happened yet are absent rather than present and empty: a queued run carries no startedAt, and a run that has not succeeded carries no output. There is deliberately no completion percentage — the engine's own progress signal is unreachable from the hardened query instance, and it would describe one statement of a run made of several. Show elapsed time from startedAt instead.

id.description: Identifies this run, distinct from its output.

state.description: The last three are terminal and never change again. A cancelled run carries no error: the user's own choice is not a fault.

warnings.description: Non-fatal facts to read before trusting the answer — today, that a measured input's coordinate system was assumed rather than declared. Present on the answer that accepts a run; the durable record is the output's own provenance, so a polled run does not repeat it.

subject.description: What groups this run with others in history. 'client' when the caller supplied the identity, 'run' when the run is its own subject.

parameters.description: The parameters this run was accepted with.

startedAt.description: Absent until the run leaves the queue.

finishedAt.description: Absent until the run reaches a terminal state.

output.description: The dataset the run wrote, by id and by name. Present only on a succeeded run.

disclosure.description: What this run asked, for a run whose answers came from a **provider** rather than the engine — the endpoint's host and path, the parameters that affected the answers, the address-normalization version, and how many distinct questions were answered from the cache and how many from the wire. It stands in place of the SQL an in-engine run records, and it belongs to *this* run: a later re-run of the same step publishes its own. The endpoint's query string, where a key travels, is never included. Absent on a run that asked nobody.

error.description: Present only on a failed run.

StaleCause.description: Why a step's output no longer reflects what it was made from. **Every active cause is reported**, each naming the input it came from: a step can read a refreshed table *and* sit downstream of a re-run step at once, and discarding one to show the other would leave this unable to say why.

producedByStepId.description: The step that produces that table, when one does.

editRevision.description: Opaque durable revision paired with this document state. Camera and derived writes do not change it.

lastChangedAt.description: Time of the last accepted covered change, independent of camera and cache clocks.

lastChangedBy.description: A named actor has display and fixed SQL names. { deleted: true } explicitly identifies a deleted actor and carries no names or profile fields. Null explicitly means unknown. Never inferred from ownership.

lastChangedBy.description: A named actor has display and fixed SQL names. { deleted: true } explicitly identifies a deleted actor and carries no names or profile fields. Null explicitly means unknown. Never inferred from ownership.

parameters.description: What the step means now — what its output was produced from. Non-scalar parameters are kept as sent.

summary.description: One line describing what this step does, composed from the operation and its active parameters — "500 m around stations". Served so every surface and every agent reads the same sentence rather than composing its own; it describes what the step means now, never a proposal awaiting a run.

proposedParameters.description: An edit awaiting a successful run; null when there is none.

output.description: The output of the run this view describes: the caller's own latest output of the step when they have one, else the workflow owner's, each runner's output being their own dataset. The step's conditions, inputs and last success describe the same run. Shown when the caller reaches the dataset; one since deleted only to its runner and the workflow's owner. Null when neither has produced one or the caller does not reach it.

runner.description: The person whose run produced it.

runId.description: The workflow run that produced it, when recorded.

jobId.description: The step's attempt that produced it, when recorded.

condition.description: The first condition true of it, in the order broken, output missing, output unavailable, stale, never run, current — un-runnable before un-current, because offering a re-run that cannot succeed tells the user the wrong thing. `output_missing`: the output of the run described was deleted. `output_unavailable`: that output exists but is outside the caller's reach (the workflow owner's, shown to a caller with no output of their own); it is named nowhere.

conditions.description: **Every** condition true of it. Conditions coexist: a step can have lost both an input and its output.

missingInputs.description: What it lost, when it is broken — with the id and name it recorded, which is how the row explains itself after a deletion. `throughStepId` is set when the break arrived from a producer upstream rather than from this step's own input. Conditions are read within the caller's reach: an input the caller cannot reach is missing to them, named as written, and for a caller whose own space is not the workflow's SQL home it carries `message`, the sentence a resource evaluation gives, the same for a hidden and a nonexistent dataset.

origin.description: Where a layer-authored step's SQL came from, including `substitutionNote` when the layer aggregated and the step took the rows behind the cells instead. The map and layer it names are left out when the caller does not reach that map.

inputs.description: The tables this step read when it last published — from the parse of the SQL that ran, never a scan of its text. Only the ones the caller reaches, and, to the workflow's owner, ones since deleted.

reads.description: What the step would read on its next run: its pending definition's reads when it holds one, its active definition's otherwise — named inputs, or the tables its SQL names — before any run and whether or not those tables exist. Present tense; `inputs` is the recorded past.

latestAttempt.description: Its most recent run, in one of the five job states. Read together with the condition and never instead of it.

templateResult.description: Set when the output this step's view describes is a template's bundled result that came with a copy of the template (its dataset's source is `template`). No run of this workflow made it, so `lastSuccessAt` is null and the output names no job or run. The step's first run replaces it, and this is null from then on.

lastChangedBy.description: A named actor has display and fixed SQL names. { deleted: true } explicitly identifies a deleted actor and carries no names or profile fields. Null explicitly means unknown. Never inferred from ownership.

origin.description: Which surface made it: the workflows page lists `workflow`; the builder's one-step Tools make `builder`. Fixed at creation.

projectId.description: The project this workflow is in: on the caller's own workflow always, a project they no longer reach included (they withdraw it with PATCH /api/projects/{id}/members), and on anyone else's the project through which the caller reaches it; null = in no project.

home.description: The SQL name of the workflow's SQL home: the account whose datasets its plain table names mean, whoever reads or runs it.

updatedAt.description: When it was last edited: rename, or a step added, edited, reordered or removed. A run is not an edit, and neither is a refused change. Strictly increasing.

RecipeSummary.description: The recipe's one-line state, computed by the server so the workflows page and an agent read the same classification. The first status that applies wins; a step in more than one condition counts once, in the status shown.

sources.description: Distinct tables read that no step of this recipe produces.

liveOutputs.description: Outputs whose dataset currently exists — what deleting the recipe leaves behind.

status.description: In precedence: `empty` (no steps); `cannot_run` (a step is broken); `in_progress` (a latest attempt queued or running); `failed` (a latest attempt failed); `run_again` (an output deleted or stale, or a pending edit); `never_run` (no step has an output); `partly_never_run` (some have none); `up_to_date`. A cancelled attempt alone changes nothing.

count.description: How many steps the status counts; 0 for empty and up to date.

applied.description: `active` changed what the step means; `proposed` is waiting on a successful run of it.

output.description: The step's output, by its recorded identity; null for a step that declared none.

state.description: `exists`: the dataset remains; `deleted`: it was produced but has since been deleted; `never`: the step never produced one.

readers.description: The recipe's other steps whose present reads name the output.

outputsRemain.description: True only when the dataset exists.

discarded.description: Whether a pending edit was there to discard.

LayoutPosition.description: Canvas units at the canvas's natural zoom.

LayoutNote.description: A layout-only annotation: no reads, no output, no state, no place in a run. Nothing in the recipe refers to it.

id.description: Chosen by the writer; unique within the document.

text.description: Markdown, at most 4,000 characters, stored verbatim. The canvas reads a `label:` line in a leading `---` block as the note's label; the API interprets nothing.

RecipeLayoutInput.description: The whole document. An absent map or list is the empty one.

steps.description: A position per step, keyed by step id.

sources.description: A position per source, keyed by table name. A source may be positioned that no step reads yet: a loose table on the canvas lives only here.

notes.description: At most 100, in the writer's order.

updatedAt.description: When the document was last written; null for one never written.

editRevision.description: Opaque durable revision paired with this document state. Camera and derived writes do not change it.

outputsRemain.description: Always true: a recipe's datasets survive its deletion.

RecipeRunAttempt.description: What became of a member's attempt: the job's state, error, times and output, composed from the live job while it is in flight — so `queued` is told from `running` — and kept with the run once it settles, so the run still says why a member failed after the node's own history is pruned. A member never attempted (`not_run`, or refused at admission) has none.

output.description: Null when the caller does not reach the dataset.

operation.description: The node's operation when the run was planned, kept with the run after the node is removed.

name.description: The name the node was called by when the run was planned — its dataset's, or the one it declared — kept after the node is removed.

output.description: The dataset this member published; null until it has.

state.description: `not_run` is the member's own condition and never a job state: nothing was minted for it.

jobId.description: The operation run this member minted; null for `not_run`.

stoppedBy.description: What stopped it — the step id of the member whose failure blocked it, or a coded reason.

stoppedReason.description: The server's own sentence for that stop, where there is one — for a member refused before any job existed, this is the only field that names *which* input was missing or which parameter was out of range. `stoppedBy` carries a code, a blocking step id or `cancelled`, none of which a reader can act on by itself.

RecipeRun.description: A recipe run is **not** an operation run. An operation run names exactly one output; this may produce several, none, or a mix of succeeded and never-attempted members — so it has its own outcome and *contains* runs rather than being one.

outcome.description: Null while it is still going. `interrupted` is how a run the server stopped mid-flight settles — it always reaches a terminal outcome, and nothing is resumed.

outputs.description: Every dataset this run produced: its runner's own.

runner.description: A named actor has display and fixed SQL names. { deleted: true } explicitly identifies a deleted actor and carries no names or profile fields. Null explicitly means unknown. Never inferred from ownership.

wide.description: True when this would carry other steps with it. The `when_wide` confirmation is about exactly this.

srid.description: Declared source SRID, or 4326 for inherent WGS84. Null when absent or unresolved.

label.description: Source CRS short name for the record sentence; artifacts always hold WGS84 coordinates.

nonNull.description: Non-NULL inputs, or complete pairs, in the sampled reader rows.

readable.description: Sampled readable inputs. Null when an optional validator is unavailable, never an invented zero.

degreeCompatible.description: Whether retained source coordinates fit degree ranges: full-input evidence for decoded geometry and eligible name matches, sampled evidence for numeric hints. A declared projected source may be false while its transformed output safely applies. Null for unvalidated hints.

reasons.description: Reasons preventing automatic use, including partial readability, unsafe placement, CRS conflicts, unavailable H3 or numeric/axis ambiguity.

orientations.description: Possible longitude/x and latitude/y roles; two entries mean ambiguous axes.

sourceRetained.description: False when a selected named-WKT source was replaced. Its original name is historical evidence, not a selectable stored column.

unreadableCount.description: Unreadable non-NULL selected inputs over the full input, not the recognition sample. Missing pair members are not unreadable.

GeometryChoice.description: One exact source column, or two distinct numeric or text-typed coordinate columns in x/y order for pair. Numeric text is read tolerantly per row on preview, first set, change and URL replay. Non-null unreadable pairs keep null geometry and are counted; either missing member is a missing input. H3 and GeoJSON forbid epsg. Omission honors declared/inherent CRS, otherwise assumes WGS84. An explicit EPSG is a user declaration; a differing existing declaration refuses. The first projection correction on native/consumed assumed geometry names the stored geometry column and its historical format (wkb without one), with epsg. No further correction is available without retained source values.

expectedRevision.description: Opaque token binding table identity and artifact generation. Do not interpret or construct it.

revision.description: Opaque token binding table identity and artifact generation. Do not interpret or construct it.

currentChoice.description: A replayable retained choice, including reconstructable automatic recognition; null for a historical consumed source. Its presence alone does not mean a manual override is stored.

mode.description: Unmodified means no manual override. Clear removes the override; the next URL refresh resets mode to unmodified and records its fresh automatic recognition.

revision.description: Opaque token binding table identity and artifact generation. Do not interpret or construct it.

rowCount.description: Number of sampled rows, the first 50 source rows at most; not the dataset total.

unreadableCount.description: Unreadable inputs in the first 50 sampled rows, excluding missing values.

geometryType.description: Geometry class in the first 50 sampled rows.

extent.description: WGS84 bounds of the first 50 sampled rows before map simplification; null without placeable nonempty sample geometry.

degreeCompatible.description: The first 50 sampled rows' decoded nonempty source coordinates before transformation: true if every row fits degrees, false if any does not, null when none has coordinates.

revision.description: Opaque token binding table identity and artifact generation. Do not interpret or construct it.

mode.description: Unmodified means no manual override. Clear removes the override; the next URL refresh resets mode to unmodified and records its fresh automatic recognition.

extent.description: Full WGS84 west, south, east, north bounds; null without a placeable nonempty geometry.

qualifiedName.description: The name the caller would type for this dataset: its plain name when it is the caller's own, <sql name>.<name> when it is another owner's, which tells two same-named datasets apart. Present on every listing and read.

owner.description: The dataset's owner. Present on every listing and read.

sourceFilename.description: The file this table arrived as. Null for a derived table, whose output never was a file, and, to anyone but its owner, for a PostGIS snapshot, whose remote schema and table belong to its owner's connection.

geometryRecord.description: Applied automatic CSV recognition or a manual file/URL geometry choice. Null after clear or recognition without a choice; legacy absence is preserved until geometry is set.

geometryCandidates.description: Automatic CSV recognition evidence. Manual geometry edits clear this stored sample; GET geometry recomputes current candidates. Legacy absence is preserved until a correction.

headerSuspect.description: True when a CSV's detected column names betrayed a broken read: a name containing a comma (the header was never split), or most names numeric or blank (the first data row was taken as the header). Advisory only — the import succeeded and nothing is blocked. Always false for non-CSV sources and derived tables; a refresh recomputes it.

source.description: Which source created the table; "operation" for a table an operation produced; "sketch" for a table drawn on a map — its sourceParams carry mapId, mapName and layerId; "template" for a dataset a copy of a template made — its sourceParams carry the template's id (`template`) and the `version` it was copied from. A template's dataset is never refreshed: the copy is the caller's to change.

sourceParams.description: As stored for the caller's own dataset. For another owner's, null when it would name a connection (a PostGIS snapshot shows its source kind and nothing more) or a map the caller does not reach. For another owner's derived dataset, `inputs` lists only the inputs the caller reaches; its `sql` and `parameters` are as stored. Parameters that re-run the import (e.g. { url }); null for single-file uploads. Container-format tables also record { layer, group? } — the source layer and, for multi-layer imports, the shared group id; for uploads these describe provenance only, since uploads are never refreshable. For a derived table this records the operation that produced it (`operation`, the catalogue's identifier), its parameters, the SQL that ran (`sql`), its inputs by id as well as by name (`inputs`), and when it ran (`ranAt`); the inspection resolves those inputs into its own `inputs` field. A table produced by an operation that asked a **provider** carries a `disclosure` — the request it made: the endpoint's host and path (`endpoint`, null when none was recorded) and the request's other recorded facts, each operation's own — and **no `sql` at all**: its statement names a private staging path, and an absence is a better contract than a redaction that must never miss. The disclosure's endpoint is host and path only; the query string, where a key travels, is never recorded anywhere. A reader may rely on these fields as the durable provenance of the dataset: the workflow canvas's Provenance tab shows them and recomputes nothing.

importedAt.description: When this table's data was last produced — the import's last run, or for a derived table the run that wrote it.

inputs.description: For a derived table: the inputs its run recorded, resolved by the id each was recorded under. An input whose id no longer exists reads as missing — never as whatever now carries its name. Resolved within the caller's reach: the dataset's owner reads an input they no longer reach as missing, exactly as a deleted one; anyone else reads only the inputs they reach.

name.description: The name recorded when the run happened.

currentName.description: The name that id carries now, if it exists.

nameReclaimed.description: The recorded name now belongs to a different table.

sizeBytes.description: Size of the stored GeoParquet artifact in bytes; present on listings and inspections, null if the file is missing.

projectIds.description: The projects this dataset is in that the caller reaches, and for the caller's own dataset every project it is in, one they no longer reach included (they withdraw it with PATCH /api/projects/{id}/members); empty = in no project. A dataset can be in several; the order carries no meaning.

ImportResult.description: An import answer. Single-table formats answer with the created table alone. Container formats (Shapefile zip, GeoPackage, KML/KMZ) can hold several layers: the answer is then the first created table plus `tables` — every table the import created, one per spatial layer — and `skipped`, the members that did not become tables and why.

PgConnection.description: A saved PostGIS connection. Passwords are write-only and never appear here.

status.description: Derived from the persisted last use. Connected becomes not_checked_lately at seven days.

postgisVersion.description: The most recently observed PostGIS version, or null when none has been observed or PostGIS was absent.

LegendCorner.description: Where the map legend sits, on the builder canvas and the published view alike. Null means bottom-left — the historical position. Overlays sharing a corner stack.

LegendOrder.description: The manual legend arrangement: layer ids in legend order, top first. Null means automatic — the legend follows the layer panel's top-to-bottom order. A write must list exactly the map's current layer ids (no misses, no strangers, no doubles) or null to return to automatic; anything else is rejected unchanged. Layers added later enter at the top until the next manual write.

BasemapAttribution.description: The active basemap's credit lines, rendered on the builder canvas and the published view; a line with an href renders as a link.

CustomBasemap.description: A per-map custom basemap style: the MapLibre style URL, its optional display name, and the attribution snapshot captured server-side at save time — the credit that stays truthful when the style itself cannot be read later.

SanitizedIcon.description: The custom-icon sanitizer's answer: the accepted markup (byte-identical to the input when nothing needed removing), whether anything changed, the bounded drop report, and the aspect ratio the renderer derives its raster box from.

StyleInspection.description: The advisory verdict on a custom basemap style URL. valid carries the style's name, layer and source counts, and normalized attribution; the other verdicts carry a worded detail. unreachable and blocked can still be saved with force — every reader's browser fetches the style itself.

BasemapLayers.description: Per-group basemap visibility: labels, roads, borders, buildings, water, land. A missing group is visible; false hides that group on the builder canvas and the published view, on every vector basemap style — imagery (satellite) has no groups, so toggles are inert there and the imagery itself is never hidden. Null means everything is visible.

MapNote.description: The map's one optional info box, shown in a map corner on the builder canvas and the published view. The body supports a safe formatting subset — bold, italic, links, lists, paragraphs; raw HTML renders as plain text and links open in a new tab. Null means no box.

Viewport.description: The map camera: pitch 0 to 60 degrees, latitude -85.051129 to 85.051129 degrees, zoom -2 to 24, all finite and inclusive. Out-of-range submissions are refused. Accepted cameras render as stored, except coverage moves a center nearer a pole than half the canvas height toward the equator and raises zoom below log2(canvas height / 512), accounting for view padding. Older stored cameras read clamped to these bounds without a write. The viewport is one whole camera: omitted pitch and bearing store zero (flat and north-up).

MapTimeline.description: The map's docked playback timeline — at most one per map. It names the layer whose time filter is expanded into the map-docked widget with playback; the window itself stays that layer's timerange filter. The layer must be non-aggregated (points/heatmap draw real features; hex/grid cells are aggregated server-side and cannot animate) and must already carry a timerange filter on the field. Null means no timeline is docked.

field.description: The temporal field — must match one of the layer's timerange filters.

speed.description: Sweep-speed multiplier (0.25–32); 1 crosses the extent at the base rate. Defaults to 1.

MapWidget.description: One dashboard card: a formula (headline aggregate), category (top 5 + Other ranking; clicking a row EXCLUDES it), histogram (distribution with a brushable range), or note (authored title + body, no data). Data types are computed server-side over their layer's effective query. field is the aggregated/grouping/binned field (null for a count formula and for notes); agg is count | sum | avg | min | max (category ranking allows count | sum | avg; histogram and note ignore it — send count); aggField is the field a category sum/avg ranks by (null otherwise); unit/note/format are formula presentation (note doubles as a note widget's body); layerId is null exactly for notes.

layerId.description: The layer the widget reads — and the only layer its selection filters. Null for notes.

note.description: Formula: caption under the number; note widget: the body (≤ 2000).

WidgetList.description: The map's widgets, in rail order (at most 12).

WidgetSelections.description: Ephemeral cross-filter state: at most one entry per widget — {widgetId, kind: 'exclude', values} names a category widget's DEACTIVATED categories (all categories are active by default; Other and unlisted categories stay); {widgetId, kind: 'range', min, max} is a histogram brush (null bounds are open-ended). The filtered field resolves from the stored widget, never the request. Selections live on the request and are never stored.

WidgetValues.description: Batched widget values. FillPaint.description: A color paint, serving the fill and the data-driven outline: {type: 'constant', color} · categorical {attribute, palette, map: [{value, color}], other} · ramp {type: 'quantile', attribute, palette, method: quantile|equal|natural|custom, breaks, colors, optional classes} (breaks strictly ascending, one fewer than colors) · continuous {type: 'continuous', attribute, palette, domain: [low, high], stops, optional clamp: [low, high], log, center, positions, reversed} (values interpolate smoothly along the stops over the domain; clamp narrows the effective domain, values outside take the end colors; log needs a strictly positive effective domain; center splits the ramp for diverging reads and starts at the mean when a diverging palette is applied). Colors are {r, g, b, a}. Computed breaks come back as nice rounded values. To set custom class boundaries, write the ramp with method: 'custom', your breaks, and baseMethod naming the method they derived from (quantile|equal|natural) — a later class-count change recomputes from it. When a low-cardinality result can realize fewer visible classes, classes remembers the requested count.

CustomPalette.description: A saved custom palette: a named gradient of ordered color stops, instance-global, usable wherever palettes are offered (continuous and classified). Styles reference it by name but bake resolved colors in, so deleting a palette never breaks a map that used it.

name.description: Stable id, assigned on save; use as `palette`.

PaletteOffer.description: Everything the palette picker offers: the curated catalogue and the saved custom palettes.

SizeScale.description: Numeric attribute → pixel-size mapping. `domain` is the attribute's value range (low, high) over the effective result, resolved server-side; `range` is the output in pixels (smallest, largest). Point radius maps area-honestly (square root of the value); line width maps linearly. Features with a missing or non-numeric value draw at the smallest size.

Aggregate.description: What each cell shows: {fn: 'count'}, or {fn: 'sum' | 'avg' | 'min' | 'max', attribute} over a numeric attribute.

Viz.description: How the layer's result is drawn. `points` (default) draws the raw features. `hexbin` and `grid` aggregate points into cells server-side — results beyond the render cap stay renderable; cells expose `value` and `count`, colored by the viz `fill` (assigned automatically when omitted). `heatmap` draws point density. `arc` and `line` draw each row as an origin→destination pair from the mapped endpoints — arc as a curved swing with an adjustable height, line straight; the path's source color and width ride the style's stroke channels, and `targetColor` blends toward the destination. `icon` draws points as a glyph from the curated bundled set — size rides the style's point-radius channel, color its fill channel, fixed or by attribute. `cluster` aggregates points client-side into count-labeled bubbles by a pixel radius; zooming in dissolves them; clicking a bubble zooms toward where it breaks apart. Non-point layers keep simple rendering. hexbin/grid may carry `elevation`: cells extrude by an aggregate — count, or a function over a numeric field — so color and height can encode different things; the aggregate's range is resolved server-side and maps linearly onto [0, height] meters. Absent = flat, exactly as before.

cellKm.description: hexbin/grid: cell edge length in **web-mercator** kilometres — a length on the map projection, not a ground distance. Web mercator stretches by 1/cos(latitude), so a 1.2 km cell covers about 730 m of ground at 52°N and about 410 m at 70°N. Any value 0.02-1000 (hexbin: hexagon edge; grid: square edge). Every other distance in this API — a buffer radius, a measured length — is ground metres.

elevation.description: hexbin/grid cell extrusion. height = the tallest prism in meters (100-20000); domain is resolved server-side — send aggregate and height only.

radiusPx.description: heatmap: kernel radius in pixels (1-200). cluster: clustering radius in pixels (20-120).

weight.description: heatmap: numeric attribute weighting each point; null = 1.

height.description: arc: swing relative to the endpoint distance (0.1-2).

targetColor.description: arc/line: destination end of the color gradient as {r, g, b, a}; omit for one fixed color.

glyph.description: icon: the glyph name from the curated Maki subset (e.g. 'cafe', 'parking', 'marker').

customSvg.description: icon: sanitized custom SVG markup; when present it wins over the glyph, tinted by the fill channel like any glyph. Writes pass through the sanitizer — scripts, event handlers and references are stripped and reported (preview via /api/icons/sanitize); not-SVG, oversize (256 KB), and nothing-drawable inputs answer invalid_request. Null clears back to the glyph.

color.description: cluster: 'fixed' paints the style's fill color; an Aggregate ({fn} or {fn, attribute}) colors bubbles on a sequential ramp over the current view's values.

showCounts.description: cluster: draw the count label on each bubble.

OdEndpoint.description: One arc/line endpoint: a geometry column of the layer's result ({kind: 'geometry', field}) or a pair of numeric longitude/latitude columns ({kind: 'lonlat', lon, lat}). Null = not yet mapped; the layer asks instead of rendering. The fields endpoint lists `geometryColumns`; numeric columns come from `filterable`.

LayerFilter.description: A structured refinement of the layer's result, applied before aggregation. Range: {field, kind: 'range', min, max} (numbers; a null bound is open-ended). Time range: {field, kind: 'timerange', min, max} (ISO-8601 strings, e.g. '2021-03-01' or '2021-03-01T08:30:00'; for date/timestamp fields). Value set: {field, kind: 'values', values} (an empty set matches nothing); with exclude: true the set inverts — keep everything EXCEPT these values (NULL rows drop, as SQL's NOT IN decides).

exclude.description: values kind only: invert the set.

min.description: Number for range, ISO-8601 string for timerange.

max.description: Number for range, ISO-8601 string for timerange.

FieldStats.description: A field's extent and distribution (numeric and time fields) or distinct values (text; bounded, by frequency), for seeding filter controls and the ramp's distribution. Time extents are ISO-8601 strings. On an aggregated (hex/grid) layer, `value` and `count` answer over the effective query — the same values classification sees.

min.description: Number for numeric, ISO-8601 string for time.

max.description: Number for numeric, ISO-8601 string for time.

bins.description: Row counts over equal bins across [min, max] — the distribution histogram behind a range brush. Empty when the extent is missing or a single value.

Style.description: A layer's full visual definition. Constant channels plus data-driven ones: `strokeBy` drives the outline color like `fill` drives the fill; `pointRadiusBy` and `strokeWidthBy` drive the sizes. Absent data-driven members mean the constant siblings apply.

fillOpacity.description: 0-1 fill translucency; 1 = opaque. Colors are solid — the sliders own alpha. Default 1.

stroke.description: Constant outline color {r, g, b, a}.

strokeOpacity.description: 0-1 multiplier on the stroke alpha. Default 1.

strokeBy.description: Data-driven outline color; overrides `stroke` when present.

heightBy.description: Polygon extrusion by attribute: the domain maps linearly onto meters (range up to 100000; resolve with the scale operation, unit 'm'). Omit for flat.

label.description: Text labels on the layer; omit for none. On a simple-feature layer set `attribute` to the column whose value labels each feature (points at the point, lines and polygons at an interior anchor). On an aggregated hex/grid layer omit `attribute` — each cell labels itself with its aggregate value, compactly formatted. Heatmaps cannot be labeled.

attribute.description: Label source column; omit on aggregated layers.

size.description: Text size, 1-72; 12 is a good default. On simple layers this is screen pixels. On hex/grid layers it scales the label's proportion of its cell — cell labels zoom with the map, like the cells themselves.

color.description: Text color {r, g, b, a}. Pick against the basemap: white reads well on dark styles and imagery, a dark color on light styles.

haloWidth.description: Halo rim behind the text, 0 (none) to 3 (widest). Replaced the legacy `halo` boolean: stored maps migrate on read; writes stating the boolean answer invalid_request.

anchor.description: One of the nine compass positions plus center, relative to the feature's anchor point; absent = center.

maxChars.description: Truncate to N code points with an ellipsis (not counted), 1 to 80; null/absent = no truncation.

density.description: Collision-culling density, 0 sparse to 1 dense; absent = 0.5. Table-backed layers only — tiled layers are exempt from thinning.

zoomFloor.description: Show labels from this whole zoom level (0-24); null/absent = no floor.

priorityField.description: Numeric column ranking which labels survive the cap and collisions (higher wins; nulls last); null/absent = stable feature order. Published maps carry the column's values.

cap.description: Draw at most N labels (1-10000), after ranking; null/absent = no cap.

sql.description: Only one read-only SELECT over named datasets is accepted. File readers, file-relation shorthand and engine path or definition discovery are refused before binding with sql_rejected, including nested SQL and computed targets. File-referencing PROJ coordinate definitions are also refused before native projection use, including computed or per-row values; EPSG identifiers and inline definitions without files remain supported. Engine errors do not expose filesystem paths or internal statements; input positions are retained when available. Existing saved SQL is retained unchanged; affected saved and published queries fail.

Feature properties are the columns the audience reads: on a builder render, what the layer and its map use; on a published render, the effective published field set. Non-point features carry a reserved __anchor property — an interior [lng, lat] that labels anchor on; it never shows in tooltips or pop-ups.

geometryType.description: Canonical geometry family of the effective render result, independent of inline or tiled delivery. Multi-geometry variants collapse into their simple family; null means the result is empty or its family is unknown.

liveFiltered.description: True when the data ships without the layer's live filters (range/time filters on non-aggregated layers) — the builder canvas enforces them client-side, so slider and playback moves never refetch. Absent when every filter is already applied in the SQL.

error.description: Present when ok is false: why the layer cannot render right now. code is one of the documented error codes (query_timeout, sql_error, render_cap_exceeded, render_bytes_exceeded, tiler_unavailable, tile_build_failed, …) and is what truth surfaces present; message carries the detail. Both builder and published viewer show an errored layer as a visible failed state, never as silent absence.

SliderPreviewData.description: Bounded point input for transient builder slider previews. `exact` is false when `geojson` is a stable subset of the source rows. This response is never durable layer state.

LayerTiles.description: How a tiled layer stands. While `building`, poll the render endpoint. When `ready`, `url` is a {z}/{x}/{y} tile URL template (with a cache-busting version parameter), and bounds ([west, south, east, north]) with the zoom range describe the archive. A failed build reports as an errored layer instead.

kind.description: The field's family: numeric, time (date/timestamp columns), or text. Decides the matching filter kind.

geometryColumns.description: Geometry columns of the layer's own SQL result, in SELECT order — what arc/line endpoints can map to.

box.description: [west, south, east, north]; absent when empty.

Publications made before this field existed read dark until published anew. A reader may switch locally for the current page load only (the remembered per-link override was retired); the switch never changes this value, and the next load starts from it again.

basemapUrl.description: Resolved basemap style URL for the authored theme — the published page's first render uses exactly this.

basemapForTheme.description: Non-null when the basemap follows the effective theme (a genuine Auto with no deployment override): the style URL for each mode (`light`, `dark`), so a reader theme switch swaps styles without another round trip. Null for an explicit basemap or an overridden Auto. In the builder every explicit basemap stays fixed in both themes; on the published viewer the Dark and Light styles are excepted, and the reader's theme control moves them as a pair — they are the two modes. Streets and Satellite stay fixed there too.

basemapKey.description: The authored basemap choice; null = Auto. The reader's picker marks its card from this and resolves a return to Auto — the resolved URL alone cannot say whether Auto or an explicit style sharing that URL was authored. Note the published Dark/Light exception described on `basemapForTheme`: a reader's theme control moves those two as a pair.

customBasemap.description: The map's custom basemap style; null = none. When set, basemapUrl is its URL in both themes, the attribution is its saved snapshot, and the reader's picker marks no built-in card — a reader who switches to one has no way back within the load.

basemapPinned.description: Whether this deployment pins Auto in both themes. A reader's theme switch leaves a pinned Auto alone; an explicit reader pick still applies for that page load.

basemapKind.description: The resolved style's kind — group toggles act on vector styles only.

timeline.description: The docked playback timeline, resolved for the viewer: layerId, field, speed, the settled window, the field's full extent (ISO-8601), and its histogram bins. Null when no timeline is docked or the dock no longer resolves.

layers.description: Each layer carries its style, render data, and `liveFilters`: resolved range/time filters the render shipped without — the viewer enforces their settled ranges client-side.

widgets.description: The map's visible widgets, present when the map ships widgets — the viewer reads values through the published widget-values call. Empty when the toggle is off or no widget resolves.

viewerControls.description: Which optional reader controls this publication exposes. A publication that never stated a set reports every control on.

qualifiedName.description: The name the caller would type: the plain name for the caller's own dataset, <sql name>.<name> for another owner's.

projectIds.description: The projects this dataset is filed in that the caller owns or belongs to, and for the caller's own dataset every project it is filed in, one they no longer reach included (they withdraw it with PATCH /api/projects/{id}/members); never another person's membership in a project the caller does not reach. Identities only; the projects listing names those the caller reaches.

AssistantContext.description: Optional page grounding, at most 64 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Omission makes no page claim. Unknown fields, malformed snapshots and incompatible object ownership refuse before work with assistant_context_invalid; oversized context answers 413 assistant_context_too_large. Server-owned identities are checked against this instance. SQL is an exact browser-submitted snapshot, not a draft write, execution or approval. A table preview is not a last execution.

appearance.description: The builder's resolved theme, so an automatic map check renders the appearance the person is looking at. Absent means light.

AssistantSqlResultSummary.description: The result of this exact executed SQL. Returned rows cannot exceed total rows. No row samples are submitted as automatic grounding.

collection.description: True when a narrower identity cannot be established.

AssistantSubject.description: The subject of an action as resolved when it happened: its resource, its identity when the call or response named one, and its display name when one was carried. A later rename or deletion does not change it.

AssistantHistory.description: Where a change qualifies for a map's history: the map and the change group the turn stamped. A turn may touch several maps and a manual edit during a pause splits its steps, so a group is the turn's marker, never a claim that it is one currently undoable step.

AssistantObservation.description: The observation attached to a map check: a separate fact recorded when the model's subsequent text arrived, never a change to the check's outcome. awaited: the check settled and the text has not come; captured: text holds the first subsequent sentence, at most 240 characters cut at a word boundary, and at is where in the run's text it begins; silent: the turn completed with no subsequent text; interrupted: no text will come, reason says why (cancelled, exhausted, failed); unavailable: the terminal compaction dropped the detail. Absence of this object on a check that did not succeed means the check produced no image.

AssistantAction.description: A known attempted action, never a raw tool-result body. Effects describe possible resources. Status distinguishes success, accepted asynchronous work (jobId), refusal and uncertainty. Additive facts recorded when the action happened: elapsedMs measures the dispatch alone, never a gate's wait; history names the map and change group of a qualifying change and is absent for excluded ones; decision says how a resolution settled a gated call; omitted marks an action whose arguments the terminal compaction dropped, so unavailable detail is never shown as empty. Missing text is covered by the receipt's incomplete flag. A map check carries render, its facts without bytes, observation, the separate later fact with its lifecycle, and automatic when the loop scheduled it itself. A terminal compaction may have dropped the render's detail lists, which is why this render's state has them optional while the check's own response does not.

label.description: The record's line for the action, composed from the operation's declared display when it happened.

AssistantConfirmationRecord.description: A settled confirmation, kept in the receipt when its pending representation goes: the exact action and the words as presented, with the decision. Approved and declined settle through a resolution; superseded through a newer message naming it or a release. Approval's outcome is the action's own record entry, failure included.

callId.description: The tool-call id the gate held; absent from the actions when the continuation stopped before the call ran.

omitted.description: The terminal compaction dropped this gate's arguments; the decision and the words stand.

AssistantPendingAction.description: Exact open action, bound to the original run and target. A confirmation resolution uses id, while recovery uses runId. Confirmation words remain those presented when the action parked.

callId.description: The tool-call id the gate holds: the action it runs as on approval, so a settled gate can be matched with its action or seen to have run as none.

AssistantModelChoice.description: A model a request may choose on this instance. The effort levels are that model's own, in its provider's own words as Dezfil knows them: there is no shared scale, and no equivalence of computational work across models or providers is claimed. Every model offers the entry "default": the provider's own no-choice behavior, which is what a request with no effort resolves to. A model Dezfil knows no levels for offers that entry alone, which states what Dezfil supports and never that the provider lacks the capability. This list is exactly the accepted set: every value here is accepted for this model, and no other value is.

id.description: The identity a request names in choice.model.

name.description: A display name; an identity with no display name reads as itself.

value.description: The word a request names in choice.effort.

AssistantCatalogueState.description: The current local model catalogue. The optional assistant-models.json in DEZFIL_DATA_DIR adds and overrides entries. A missing or rejected copy uses shipped knowledge; a valid copy, including an empty one, reports merged. A rejection reason names the invalid field or read failure without file contents. Each enabled status read and new message admission reads the current files.

AssistantProvenance.description: What a run asked for and what its provider answers reported. Two separate facts: a requested setting is never evidence of the reasoning work a provider actually did.

requested.description: The pair the first accepted submission bound, written before any provider request exists, so a run that fails before an answer still reports it. effort is "default" where none was chosen.

defaulted.description: Which halves the instance supplied rather than the requester.

reported.description: The distinct identities completed provider responses reported, in first-seen order; a null entry is a response that completed reporting none. Absent means no provider response completed at all, which is not the same fact as a response that named nothing.

AssistantPolicy.description: A page's action policy and default offer. admitted is every operation a run under the page may call; offered is what its model is shown at the start, the discovery tool included when discovery is on; discovery says whether the admitted operations outside the offer are reachable through it. offer names the mode: subset (the page's operations and the grounding reads) or full (every admitted operation).

AssistantRun.description: Read-only progress snapshot. Observation starts no work and cannot resume an interrupted run. Working state is lost on process replacement.

confirmations.description: Settled confirmations of this run, in order.

catalogue.description: Present when enabled; absent when disabled.

autoCheck.description: Present when enabled: whether the assistant checks the map by itself after a turn that changed it. The instance owner's setting, DEZFIL_ASSISTANT_AUTO_CHECK, on by default; 0, false or off turns it off. An explicit check is available whatever this says.

models.description: Present when enabled: every model a request may choose on this instance, the resolved provider's list alone, with the default among them exactly once. The instance owner narrows and orders it with DEZFIL_AI_MODELS_ANTHROPIC or DEZFIL_AI_MODELS_OPENAI. Unset offers the effective catalogue in file order. A set empty or separators-only list offers the default alone. The default stays where listed or is prepended when missing. Unknown identities read as themselves with default effort alone. Listing an identity grants permission to request it; whether the provider has it is the provider's own answer.

AssistantRequest.description: Either a message (optionally with history and a superseded pending action) or a resolution, never both.

runId.description: Identity obtained before submission from POST /api/assistant/runs.

history.description: Prior turns as {role, text}; conversations are not stored server-side.

supersedes.description: A pending-action id this message abandons (the implicit decline). Unknown ids are ignored.

choice.description: Optional: the model and the effort this run is sent to, both optional inside it. An omitted model is the instance default; an omitted effort is the selected model's provider-default entry; an empty choice is an omission. GET /api/assistant reports what this instance offers. The first accepted submission binds the pair for the whole run, tool continuations, confirmation continuations and the map check's observation included; a choice supplied on a resolution is ignored, as a context supplied there already is. A malformed choice (400 assistant_choice_invalid), a model this instance does not offer (400 assistant_model_not_offered), an effort the selected model does not offer (400 assistant_effort_not_offered) and a named level for a model that has no levels of its own (400 assistant_effort_not_supported) are each refused before the run binds and before any provider call or product operation, leaving the reservation unbound and reusable. The entry "default" is accepted for every offered model and resolves exactly as omitting the effort does; the two differ only in what provenance.requested.defaulted records.

model.description: An identity from the status read's models.

effort.description: One of that model's own effort values, "default" among them.

oneOf.title: Resolution
oneOf.description: Resolve the confirmation a confirm_required event raised, instead of sending a message. Binds to the server-issued pending-action id; at most one resolution ever takes effect. Any context supplied on a resolution is ignored; the run retains its original context while server-owned facts are refreshed.

AssistantEvent.description: One streamed event. text_delta carries an incremental text chunk and messageId; message carries the complete text for that same messageId. Legacy clients ignore deltas; delta-aware clients replace that message at completion, never append it twice. Recovery text is a replacement snapshot, not a delta. Partial tool arguments and private reasoning are not emitted or executed. Action events carry resolved effects; confirm_required carries target and consequence words. outcome distinguishes succeeded, accepted, refused and uncertain; jobId identifies accepted asynchronous work. `type` is one of text_delta, message, tool_call, tool_result, observation, confirm_required, error, done. On confirm_required, `id` is the server-issued pending-action id a resolution references (not a provider tool-call id); the run has paused and the stream ends until a resolution request continues it.

model.description: Actual provider model on a completed model message.

callId.description: On confirm_required: the provider tool-call id the gate holds.

label.description: On tool_call and tool_result: the record's line for the action.

elapsedMs.description: On tool_result: execution time around the dispatch alone.

decision.description: On the tool_result a resolution settled: how.

render.description: On a map check's tool_result: the render's facts, never its bytes.

automatic.description: On a map check's tool_call and tool_result: the loop scheduled it itself.

state.description: On observation: the observation's lifecycle state; id names the check action, text the displayed sentence, reason why none will come.

reason.description: On done: why the turn ended (end, budget, interrupted). On observation: why no observation will come (cancelled, exhausted, failed); the loop yields exhausted when the last step was spent on the check itself.

x-error-codes.invalid_link: This sign-in link is unavailable, expired, replaced or already used.
x-error-codes.token_expired: The API token has passed the expiry it was created with and no longer works. Create a new token; the expired one stays listed until it is revoked.
x-error-codes.rule_refused: An instance rule an admin sets refuses this action for the current account: creating an API token, publishing a map or changing a live publication, adding a database connection or pointing one at another host, port or database, or importing from a link. The refusal's rule field names the rule as PATCH /api/instance/settings takes it. Nothing changed, and what already exists keeps working.
x-error-codes.current_password_required: Enter your current password to make this change.
x-error-codes.authentication_busy: Authentication is busy. Try again shortly.
x-error-codes.ingress_unavailable: Trusted socket provenance is unavailable. Authentication entry and published reads cannot proceed.
x-error-codes.geometry_not_supported: Set geometry is available only for file uploads and URL imports.
x-error-codes.geometry_choice_invalid: The geometry choice cannot be applied. The message explains the projection, source or validator issue.
x-error-codes.geometry_in_flight: A geometry edit or refresh is already running for this dataset or URL import group.
x-error-codes.unsupported_format: The uploaded file type is not one of the supported formats.
x-error-codes.unsupported_image: The picture is not a still JPEG, PNG or WebP image: another kind, an animated image, or one that is damaged or incomplete. Nothing changed.
x-error-codes.image_too_large: The picture has more pixels than the fixed limit of 64 million, read from its header before any pixel is decoded. Nothing changed.
x-error-codes.upload_too_large: The upload exceeds its size cap: the configured upload cap, or a picture's fixed 10 MB.
x-error-codes.archive_too_large: The archive's unpacked content exceeds the configured upload size cap.
x-error-codes.remote_fetch_failed: The remote file could not be fetched (unreachable, denied, or missing).
x-error-codes.remote_fetch_abandoned: The outbound request was abandoned before it finished, because whoever asked for it stopped waiting.
x-error-codes.remote_too_large: The remote file exceeds the configured remote size cap.
x-error-codes.remote_timeout: The remote fetch exceeded the configured remote time bound.
x-error-codes.egress_blocked: The destination address is blocked by the egress policy (loopback, private, link-local, or metadata space); the configured allowlist admits exceptions.
x-error-codes.imagery_unavailable: The satellite imagery did not answer a tile the instance relays with one: it could not be reached, its address is refused by the egress policy, it answered an error, too slowly, past the size bound or with something other than a raster image, or its tile address carries a user name or password and is not drawn. The message says which, never the tile address or its key.
x-error-codes.area_too_large: The selected area exceeds the import budget for the chosen theme.
x-error-codes.name_taken: A table of that name already exists. Operations never replace or rename around an existing table. Choose another name.
x-error-codes.not_refreshable: The table has no re-runnable remote source, so it cannot be refreshed.
x-error-codes.dependencies_unresolved: A layer's statement could not be analyzed, so the map's datasets cannot be listed completely. Fix the layer's SQL and try again.
x-error-codes.export_failed: The project archive could not be assembled; nothing was delivered. Retry, and check the server's disk space if it recurs.
x-error-codes.refresh_in_flight: A refresh of this table (or its OSM import group) is already running; retry when it completes.
x-error-codes.connection_failed: The database connection failed (unreachable, authentication, or missing extension).
x-error-codes.connection_password_required: Enter the password again when changing the host or port, or turning SSL off.
x-error-codes.malformed_file: The file could not be parsed as its declared format.
x-error-codes.request_body_too_large: The request body exceeds its documented byte limit.
x-error-codes.mcp_read_failed: The read could not be completed because its response could not be received.
x-error-codes.mcp_transport_failed: The operation's response could not be received. Its outcome is unknown.
x-error-codes.mcp_response_invalid: The instance returned a response that does not match this operation's documented result.
x-error-codes.stale_revision: This item has changed. Reload it before trying again.
x-error-codes.invalid_request: The request was malformed or failed validation, including a missing or malformed required edit revision. Read the item before a covered write.
x-error-codes.not_found: The requested resource was not found.
x-error-codes.sql_rejected: The SQL was not an accepted read-only query.
x-error-codes.sql_error: The SQL failed to parse or execute.
x-error-codes.query_timeout: The query exceeded the configured timeout.
x-error-codes.engine_memory_exceeded: Trusted data work exceeded its shared memory or scratch budget. Reduce the work, or raise DEZFIL_TRUSTED_MEMORY_MB and restart.
x-error-codes.data_processing_timeout: Data processing exceeded its admitted time limit. An admin can change Data processing time limit for new work; a picture's limits are fixed.
x-error-codes.request_timeout: The request body was not received within 300 s.
x-error-codes.upload_stalled: The upload sent no body bytes for 60 seconds. Retry the upload.
x-error-codes.render_bytes_exceeded: The features to draw exceed the configured byte limit.
x-error-codes.query_memory_exceeded: The query exceeded the configured engine memory budget for user SQL.
x-error-codes.query_result_too_large: The result is too large to return: more than 32 MB in total, or one non-geometry value over 2 MB. Select fewer rows or columns, or shorten the value.
x-error-codes.tile_build_timeout: A tile-build stage exceeded the configured tile-build timeout.
x-error-codes.render_cap_exceeded: The layer's result exceeds the inline render cap; tiled rendering is unavailable for this geometry or configuration.
x-error-codes.tiler_unavailable: The result is too large for inline rendering and no tile builder is installed on this instance.
x-error-codes.tile_build_failed: The layer's tile archive could not be built.
x-error-codes.render_unavailable: The image renderer's browser is not available on this instance, so image export cannot run.
x-error-codes.render_timeout: The image render exceeded the configured export render budget (queue wait included).
x-error-codes.render_failed: The image could not be rendered. Retry; if it persists, the instance's renderer needs attention.
x-error-codes.look_target_missing: No map was named for the check and none is in context, so there is nothing to render.
x-error-codes.look_image_too_large: No image of the map fits inside the check's byte bound at any documented size, so none was returned.
x-error-codes.look_image_unavailable: The image of this check is no longer kept on this instance: it was evicted under the retention bounds or did not survive a restart. It is never rendered again.
x-error-codes.attachment_too_large: The tool attachment exceeds the configured cap; narrow the export or raise the cap.
x-error-codes.operation_timeout: The operation exceeded the configured execution budget for a run. Time spent waiting for the lane is not counted against it.
x-error-codes.operation_queue_full: Too many operations are already queued; the run was refused rather than accepted into a queue that would not drain. Retry once some complete.
x-error-codes.run_in_flight: This workflow already has a run in flight; a workflow runs one at a time. Wait for it, or cancel it, then run again.
x-error-codes.plan_changed: The workflow changed since the run was confirmed, so the nodes it would run are not the ones confirmed. Nothing started; look at the plan again.
x-error-codes.operation_interrupted: The server stopped while this run was in the lane, so it did not finish. Nothing partial was kept; run it again.
x-error-codes.input_changed: An input was replaced while the run was waiting, so the answers it had prepared belong to data that is no longer there. Nothing was written; run it again against the current data.
x-error-codes.geocoder_unconfigured: No geocoding endpoint is configured on this instance (the Address finder an admin sets, or DEZFIL_GEOCODER_URL), so an operation that asks a provider for addresses cannot run. The message says which one to change now.
x-error-codes.geocoder_failed: The configured geocoding endpoint did not answer, twice in a row. The run published nothing rather than recording an absent answer as an address that does not exist.
x-error-codes.isochrone_unconfigured: No routing endpoint is configured on this instance (the travel-time endpoint an admin sets, or DEZFIL_ISOCHRONE_URL), so an operation that asks a provider for travel-time areas cannot run. The message says which one to change now.
x-error-codes.isochrone_failed: The configured routing endpoint did not answer, twice in a row. The run published nothing rather than recording an absent answer as an unreachable origin.
x-error-codes.service_address_unreadable: A service address, or the satellite imagery's tile template, an admin saved in Settings cannot be read with this instance's encryption key, which changed after it was saved. The service, or the imagery style, refuses rather than reach a default; an admin saves the address again.
x-error-codes.basemap_not_offered: The basemap a map write or an undo or redo would put a map on is one this instance does not offer now: a style an admin hid, or, while style addresses on single maps are off, a style address the basemap library does not offer. It cannot be chosen anew. The refusal's setting field names the switch, as PATCH /api/instance/settings takes it. Nothing changed; a map already on that basemap keeps it, and Auto is always offered.
x-error-codes.measurement_crs_unavailable: The data is too wide to measure a distance over in ground metres: in a projection centred on it, a distance at its widest point would be off by more than 1 %, or it crosses the antimeridian. The message names its width and extent. Split it by region and measure each part; an area over the same data succeeds and records the global projection it used.
x-error-codes.operation_superseded: The step this run belonged to was changed or removed while it was working, so the run lost its authority to publish and wrote nothing. What it would have produced is no longer what the step means.
x-error-codes.widget_layer_missing: The widget references a layer that no longer exists, so its value cannot be computed.
x-error-codes.column_unavailable: The write introduces a reference to a column the layer's result does not provide, or provides with a type the channel cannot use, so it was refused; stored references are never retro-refused.
x-error-codes.field_not_published: The selection references a field the published surface does not declare: outside the layer's effective published field set and not a published widget's field.
x-error-codes.catalogue_not_published: A published layer or widget whose SQL reads the instance's catalogue does not evaluate on the link while its owner holds datasets the map does not name: a published map reaches only the datasets its own layers name, and the link would otherwise disclose the others.
x-error-codes.selection_incompatible: The selection's values cannot be evaluated against its field's type (for example a time range on a non-time field); it was refused before evaluation.
x-error-codes.rate_limited: Too many requests or sign-in attempts; retry after the indicated delay.
x-error-codes.catalogue_too_large: The schema page exceeds 96 KiB. Request fewer tables or columns.
x-error-codes.assistant_reservation_required: Reserve a run with POST /api/assistant/runs, then send its id as runId.
x-error-codes.assistant_run_unavailable: This run identity is unavailable and cannot execute.
x-error-codes.assistant_run_conflict: This run identity is already bound to different input.
x-error-codes.assistant_capacity: Eight assistant runs occupy capacity. Read GET /api/assistant/pending; release an unused reservation or abandon a pending turn with DELETE /api/assistant/runs/{id}.
x-error-codes.assistant_run_state: This operation is not available in the current run state.
x-error-codes.assistant_recovery_limit: Further work stopped before the live recovery bound could be exceeded.
x-error-codes.assistant_plan_unavailable: The current workflow membership could not be established. No run was approved or started.
x-error-codes.assistant_action_uncertain: The action outcome could not be established. Its declared resources may have changed.
x-error-codes.assistant_action_interrupted: The read was interrupted before completion.
x-error-codes.assistant_action_not_admitted: The run's page context does not admit this operation; nothing was performed. Runs under a /sql or workflow context admit only operations that declare themselves read-only, and none that reaches outside this server or asks for confirmation.
x-error-codes.assistant_choice_invalid: The submitted model choice is malformed: it must be an object whose optional model and effort are strings.
x-error-codes.assistant_model_not_offered: The requested model is not one this instance offers. GET /api/assistant lists the models it offers.
x-error-codes.assistant_effort_not_offered: The requested effort is not one the selected model offers. GET /api/assistant lists each model's own efforts.
x-error-codes.assistant_effort_not_supported: The selected model has no effort levels of its own, so it takes only the provider default. Send the effort "default", or no effort at all, or choose a model that offers levels. GET /api/assistant lists each model's own efforts.
x-error-codes.assistant_context_invalid: The submitted page context is malformed or refers to an incompatible object.
x-error-codes.assistant_context_too_large: Page context exceeds 64 KiB of UTF-8 JSON.
x-error-codes.assistant_context_unavailable: The page context could not be read from this instance.

x-error-codes.assistant_provider: The model provider request failed (outage, quota, or network).
